definition_zh: 惊吓；恐惧；吓人的东西；怪样子
definition_en: a sudden feeling of fear, or something that causes it
core_image: 夜里突然一声巨响，人一下子缩起肩膀
scene: 深更半夜，楼道里忽然传来一声闷响，她吓得心口一紧。A sudden bang in the hallway gave her a fright.
sceneCN: 这里 fright 是「惊吓」（第 1 个义项：突如其来的恐惧）；句意：楼道里突然一声巨响，把她吓了一跳。

pos.zh: 惊吓；恐惧；吓人的东西；怪样子
使惊吓；吓唬（书面或古旧用法）

derivatives.zh: 由名词加 -en 构成，义为「使害怕；吓唬」
由 frighten 加 -ed 构成，义为「受惊的；害怕的」
由 frighten 加 -ing 构成，义为「令人恐惧的」
加 -ful 构成，义为「可怕的；糟糕透顶的」
由 frightful 加 -ly 构成，义为「极度地；非常」

senses.title: Sudden fear
senses.definition: a sudden feeling of fear caused by something unexpected
senses.definitionCN: 由意外之事引起的突如其来的恐惧
senses.example: The crash gave the children a fright.
senses.exampleCN: 那声撞击把孩子们吓了一跳。
senses.why: The Old English noun named a sudden onset of dread, and the modern word keeps that burst of fear.
senses.whyCN: 古英语名词本指突然袭来的恐惧，现代英语保留了这个「猛然一惊」的核心。

senses.title: A cause of fear
senses.titleCN: 吓人的东西；令人惊恐的事
senses.definition: a person or thing that makes someone suddenly afraid
senses.definitionCN: 使人突然害怕的人或事物
senses.example: The ruined house was a real fright to the villagers.
senses.exampleCN: 那座破败的房子真把村民吓坏了。
senses.why: From naming the feeling, the word moved to naming whatever produces it, a common shift from effect to cause.
senses.whyCN: 词从指「感受」转指「引起感受的东西」，这是由结果转向原因的常见引申。

senses.title: A ridiculous appearance
senses.definition: an appearance that looks strange, messy, or ridiculous
senses.definitionCN: 显得古怪、凌乱或滑稽的外表
senses.example: She came in out of the rain looking a fright.
senses.exampleCN: 她淋着雨进来，样子狼狈极了。
senses.why: British informal use turns the shock of fear into the shock of an odd sight.
senses.whyCN: 英式口语把「惊吓」的冲击感转到「怪样子」的视觉冲击上。

senses.title: To scare someone
senses.definition: to make someone suddenly afraid
senses.definitionCN: 使某人突然害怕
senses.example: The dog frighted the postman at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 那条狗在门口把邮递员吓了一跳。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb in Middle English, meaning to strike someone with sudden fear.
senses.whyCN: 中古英语时名词转为动词，义为以突如其来的恐惧击中某人。

intro.en: Fright goes back to Old English fyrhto, a noun for fear and trembling, from a Germanic root shared by German Furcht.
intro.cn: fright 可追溯至古英语 fyrhto（恐惧、发抖），其词根与德语 Furcht 同源。

items.en: The root furht- named fear and trembling across the Germanic languages.
items.cn: 词根 furht- 在日耳曼诸语中表示恐惧与发抖。

items.en: Fyrhto and fyrhtu mean fear, dread, and trembling.
items.cn: fyrhto 与 fyrhtu 意为恐惧、畏惧与发抖。

items.en: The noun appears as fright, with the sense of sudden alarm.
items.cn: 名词写作 fright，指突然的惊恐。

items.en: A verb fright, meaning to terrify, grows beside the noun.
items.cn: 十四世纪出现动词 fright，意为使恐惧。

items.en: Fright keeps the noun sense and survives mainly in fixed phrases and informal use.
items.cn: 现代英语的 fright 保留名词义，多用于固定搭配与口语。

note.en: Fright names a sudden fear and sits beside its own verb family and the wider field of fear words.
note.cn: fright 指突如其来的恐惧，与自己的动词词族以及更广的「恐惧」词场相邻。

entries.definition: to make someone afraid
very bad or unpleasant, or causing fear
feeling fear
extreme fear
sudden fear that cannot be controlled
fear caused by a sense of danger

normalIntro.en: Fright is a sudden shock of fear, and its family spreads outward through frighten, frightened, and frightful.
normalIntro.cn: fright 是恐惧的猛然一击，其词族经由 frighten、frightened、frightful 向外扩展。

normal.en: Fright is the noun; frighten is the verb that means to cause it.
normal.cn: fright 是名词，frighten 是表示「使害怕」的动词。

normal.en: A fright is sudden, while fear can last a long time.
normal.cn: a fright 是突如其来的，而 fear 可以持续很久。

normal.en: Stage fright is the fear of facing an audience.
normal.cn: stage fright 是面对观众时的怯场。

normal.en: Frightful describes something awful, not only something scary.
normal.cn: frightful 形容极糟的东西，而不只是吓人的东西。

normal.en: Take fright means to become frightened suddenly.
normal.cn: take fright 表示突然受惊。

abstract.en: Picture a shoulder jerking up at a sudden noise in the dark.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗中一声响，肩膀猛地一缩。

abstract.en: Think of a mask on a wall that makes a child step back.
abstract.cn: 想象墙上的一副面具，让小孩后退一步。

abstract.en: See a person arriving soaked, hair flat, clothes dripping.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人浑身湿透地进门，头发贴着额头，衣服滴水。

examples.en: The thunder gave the baby a fright.
examples.cn: 雷声把婴儿吓了一跳。

examples.en: He took fright at the sight of the dog.
examples.cn: 他一看见那条狗就害怕起来。

examples.en: The sight of the steep drop gave us a fright.
examples.cn: 看到那处陡坡，我们吓了一跳。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fright」读起来像「弗莱特」，可以联想突然被吓到而「发怵」；这只是谐音联想，并非词源。

root: 古英语 fyrhto（恐惧、发抖）→ 中古英语 fright（突然的惊恐）→ 现代英语 fright；核心义为「突如其来的恐惧」。

sensesIntro.en: Fright starts as the sudden feeling itself, then names what causes it, then an odd sight, and finally the act of scaring someone.
sensesIntro.cn: fright 先指突然的恐惧本身，再指引起恐惧的东西，继而指怪异的外表，最后指吓唬人的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shoulder jerking up at a sudden noise in the dark.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑暗中一声响，肩膀猛地一缩。

branches.en: The feeling itself is the central sense.
branches.cn: 恐惧的感受本身是中心义项。

branches.en: The cause of the feeling is a short step away from it.
branches.cn: 引起恐惧的原因是紧邻的一步引申。

branches.en: An odd sight borrows the shock of fear.
branches.cn: 怪异的外表借用了恐惧的冲击感。

branches.en: The noun and the verb name the feeling and the act that produces it.
branches.cn: 名词与动词分别指感受和造成感受的动作。

branches.en: Both a frightening thing and a ridiculous figure make the viewer start.
branches.cn: 吓人的东西与滑稽的形象都会让看的人一惊。

intro.en: Fright is a Germanic noun with an English verb family built on it: frighten, frightened, frightful, and frightfully.
intro.cn: fright 是日耳曼语名词，英语在其上构成 frighten、frightened、frightful、frightfully 等词族。

latinIntro.en: Fright has no Latin source; it comes from Old English fyrhto and the Germanic root furht-.
latinIntro.cn: fright 没有拉丁语来源，它出自古英语 fyrhto 与日耳曼语词根 furht-。

items.example: Fyrhto is the earliest recorded form of the word.
items.exampleCN: fyrhto 是这个词最早见于记录的形式。

items.example: A variant fyrhtu appears in Old English texts.
items.exampleCN: 古英语文献中还有变体 fyrhtu。

items.example: Middle English fright keeps the sense of sudden alarm.
items.exampleCN: 中古英语 fright 保留突然惊恐之义。

items.example: The bang gave her a fright.
items.exampleCN: 那声巨响把她吓了一跳。

items.example: The verb fright survives in older writing.
items.exampleCN: 动词 fright 仍见于较古的文本。

items.example: The suffix -en forms frighten from fright.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -en 由 fright 构成 frighten。

items.example: Loud noises frighten the birds.
items.exampleCN: 巨响会吓到鸟。

items.example: The suffix -ed forms frightened.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 构成 frightened。

items.example: The suffix -ful forms frightful.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ful 构成 frightful。

items.example: Frightful weather kept the boats in port.
items.exampleCN: 恶劣的天气让船只留在港内。

definition_zh: 寒冷的；严寒的；冷淡的；性冷淡的
definition_en: very cold in temperature, or cold and distant in feeling
core_image: 结霜的窗玻璃：手指一碰，寒气顺着指尖往上走
scene: 北方的清晨，窗上结满白霜，屋里的水盆冻了一层薄冰。The frigid morning air made the pipes crack.
sceneCN: 这里 frigid 是「严寒的」（第 1 个义项：气温极低）；句意：那个寒冷的清晨，空气把水管都冻裂了。

pos.zh: 寒冷的；严寒的；冷淡的；性冷淡的

derivatives.zh: 由 frigid 加 -ity 构成，义为「寒冷；冷淡；性冷淡」
由 frigid 加 -ly 构成，义为「冷淡地」
由 frigid 加 -ness 构成，义为「冷淡；寒冷」
由拉丁语 re- 加 frigerare 构成，义为「冷藏」

senses.title: Very cold
senses.definition: extremely cold in temperature
senses.definitionCN: 气温极低；非常寒冷
senses.example: The frigid wind cut through two coats.
senses.exampleCN: 寒风穿透了两层外套。
senses.why: Latin frigidus simply means cold, and this literal sense is the oldest one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 frigidus 本义就是「冷的」，这个字面义是最早的义项。

senses.title: Cold in manner
senses.definition: showing no warmth of feeling toward others
senses.definitionCN: 对他人不流露温情；态度冷淡
senses.example: Her frigid reply ended the conversation.
senses.exampleCN: 她冷淡的回答让谈话就此结束。
senses.why: Coldness of air became a metaphor for coldness of feeling.
senses.whyCN: 空气的寒冷被比附为情感的寒冷。

senses.title: Lacking sexual desire
senses.definition: having little or no sexual desire, used especially of a woman in older medical writing
senses.definitionCN: 几乎没有性欲，旧时医学文字尤用于女性
senses.example: The old textbook described her as frigid.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧教科书把她的情况描述为性冷淡。
senses.why: Medical writing of the past borrowed the cold metaphor for a lack of desire.
senses.whyCN: 旧时医学写作借「冷」的比喻来表示欲望的缺乏。

senses.title: Stiff and formal
senses.definition: stiff, formal, and without liveliness, as of style or manner
senses.definitionCN: 风格或举止僵硬、刻板、缺乏生气
senses.example: The frigid prose of the report put readers to sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 那份报告呆板的文笔让读者昏昏欲睡。
senses.why: Cold things do not move easily, so the word also pictures a style frozen stiff.
senses.whyCN: 冷的东西不易流动，所以这个词也用来形容「冻住」的僵硬文风。

intro.en: Frigid comes from Latin frigidus, cold, from frigere, to be cold, and frigus, coldness.
intro.cn: frigid 来自拉丁语 frigidus（冷的），源于 frigere（感到冷）与 frigus（寒冷）。

items.en: Frigus means cold, coldness, and chill.
items.cn: frigus 意为寒冷、冰冷。

items.en: Frigidus means cold or chilling, and also stiff.
items.cn: frigidus 意为冷的、冰冷的，也有僵硬之义。

items.en: Frigere means to be cold or to grow cold.
items.cn: frigere 意为感到冷或变冷。

items.en: English borrows the adjective as frigid, keeping the sense of cold.
items.cn: 英语借入形容词 frigid，保留「冷」的含义。

items.en: The word extends to cold manners and to medical use.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到冷淡的态度与医学用法。

items.en: A probable root for cold may also appear in Greek rhigos, shivering, but the reconstruction is uncertain.
items.cn: 一个可能表示「冷」的词根也见于希腊语 rhigos（发抖），但该重构并不确定。

note.en: Frigid belongs to the Latin cold family and to the wider field of temperature and emotional distance words.
note.cn: frigid 属于拉丁语「冷」词族，也与温度、情感疏离的词场相邻。

entries.definition: coldness, especially of feeling
in a cold and distant manner
to keep food or drink cold
having a low temperature
very cold, like ice
not friendly or close in feeling

normalIntro.en: Frigid is the Latin cold of air, water, and manner, and its family keeps the same chill.
normalIntro.cn: frigid 是拉丁语里空气、水与态度的「冷」，其词族都带着这股寒意。

normal.en: Frigid means very cold, as in frigid air and a frigid climate.
normal.cn: frigid 表示非常冷，如 frigid air 与 frigid climate。

normal.en: The frigid zone is the cold belt near the poles.
normal.cn: the frigid zone 指极地附近的寒带。

normal.en: A frigid manner feels as unwelcoming as a cold room.
normal.cn: a frigid manner 像冷屋子一样让人感到不受欢迎。

normal.en: Frigidity is the noun for coldness of body or of feeling.
normal.cn: frigidity 是表示身体或情感冷淡的名词。

normal.en: Refrigerate shares the same Latin cold: it means to keep food cold.
normal.cn: refrigerate 共享同一个拉丁语「冷」，意为冷藏食物。

abstract.en: Think of a window pane white with frost and a fingertip stuck to it.
abstract.cn: 想象窗玻璃结满白霜，指尖一碰就粘住。

abstract.en: Picture a handshake offered without a smile.
abstract.cn: 想象一次没有笑容的握手。

abstract.en: See a thermometer that refuses to rise, however warm the room.
abstract.cn: 想象一支温度计，无论屋子多暖都不肯上升。

examples.en: The frigid water numbed our feet within a minute.
examples.cn: 冰冷的水一分钟内就把我们的脚冻麻了。

examples.en: He gave a frigid nod and walked on.
examples.cn: 他冷淡地点了下头就继续走。

examples.en: Winters in the far north are more frigid than here.
examples.cn: 远北的冬天比这里更寒冷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗瑞吉德」——听起来像冷得发抖时嘟囔的声音；这只是谐音联想，并非词源。

root: 拉丁语 frigus（寒冷）→ frigere（感到冷）→ frigidus（冷的）→ 英语 frigid，核心义「冷到僵硬」。

sensesIntro.en: Frigid runs from cold temperature to cold feeling, then to a lack of desire, and finally to stiff, lifeless style.
sensesIntro.cn: frigid 从气温的冷，走到情感的冷，再到欲望的缺失，最后到僵硬无生气的风格。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: frost on a window pane, cold enough to stop a fingertip.
core.cn: 核心意象：窗玻璃上的白霜，冷得让指尖停住。

branches.en: Literal cold is the source sense.
branches.cn: 字面的「冷」是源头义项。

branches.en: Cold air easily becomes a picture of cold feeling.
branches.cn: 冷空气很容易变成冷淡情感的图景。

branches.en: Medical use takes the cold metaphor further into desire.
branches.cn: 医学用法把「冷」的比喻进一步推到欲望层面。

branches.en: A frozen thing cannot move, so cold also means stiff.
branches.cn: 冻住的东西无法活动，所以「冷」也表示僵硬。

branches.en: Both the weather sense and the style sense rest on the same chill.
branches.cn: 天气义与风格义都建立在同一股寒意上。

intro.en: Frigid is a Latin adjective whose family in English includes frigidity, frigidly, and refrigerate.
intro.cn: frigid 是拉丁语形容词，其英语词族包括 frigidity、frigidly 与 refrigerate。

latinIntro.en: Latin frigus, coldness, and frigere, to be cold, supply the whole family, including refrigerare, to make cold.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 frigus（寒冷）与 frigere（感到冷）提供了整个词族，也包括 refrigerare（使冷）。

items.example: Frigus is the noun behind the English word.
items.exampleCN: frigus 是英语这个词背后的名词。

items.example: Frigere describes the state of being cold.
items.exampleCN: frigere 描述处于寒冷之中。

items.example: Frigidus passes directly into English as frigid.
items.exampleCN: frigidus 直接进入英语成为 frigid。

items.example: Frigid describes cold air and a cold manner.
items.exampleCN: frigid 描述寒冷的空气与冷淡的态度。

items.example: The ending -id marks the adjective frigidus.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -id 标记形容词 frigidus。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ity forms frigidity.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 frigidity。

items.example: Frigidity names the state of being frigid.
items.exampleCN: frigidity 表示 frigid 的状态。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms the adverb frigidly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成副词 frigidly。

items.example: The prefix re- joins frigere in refrigerare.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 与 frigere 结合成 refrigerare。

items.example: Refrigerate the food to keep it fresh.
items.exampleCN: 把食物冷藏以保持新鲜。

definition_zh: 活泼好动的；欢蹦乱跳的；轻佻的；坐不住的
definition_en: full of lively energy and playfulness
core_image: 小狗绕着人的脚边打转，尾巴摇成一片模糊的影子
scene: 院子里，小马驹撒开腿跑圈，蹄子扬起一串尘土。The frisky foal kicked up dust as it ran.
sceneCN: 这里 frisky 是「欢蹦乱跳的」（第 1 个义项：精力旺盛、爱闹）；句意：那匹撒欢的小马跑来跑去，扬起尘土。

pos.zh: 活泼好动的；欢蹦乱跳的；轻佻的；坐不住的

derivatives.zh: 由 frisky 加 -ness 构成，义为「活泼好动」
由 frisky 变 y 为 i 加 -ly 构成，义为「活泼地」
frisky 去掉 -y 得到的基础动词，义为「欢跳；蹦来蹦去」
由 frisk 加 -ing 构成，义为「欢跳；嬉闹」

senses.title: Lively and playful
senses.titleCN: 活泼好动的；欢蹦乱跳的
senses.definition: full of energy and eager to jump, run, or play
senses.definitionCN: 精力充沛，爱跳爱跑爱玩
senses.example: The frisky puppy chased its own tail.
senses.exampleCN: 那只欢蹦乱跳的小狗追着自己的尾巴。
senses.why: The word adds -y to frisk, a verb for jumping about, so it names the mood behind the jumping.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由表示「蹦跳」的动词 frisk 加 -y 构成，指蹦跳背后的那股兴致。

senses.title: Playfully flirtatious
senses.definition: playfully bold in a romantic or sexual way
senses.definitionCN: 在浪漫或两性意味上顽皮而大胆
senses.example: His frisky remarks made her laugh and frown at once.
senses.exampleCN: 他轻佻的话让她又笑又皱眉。
senses.why: Playful energy aimed at other people turns into a light, flirtatious manner.
senses.whyCN: 「爱闹的精力」用在他人身上，就转为轻快的调情态度。

senses.title: Brisk and springy
senses.definition: quick and springy in movement, as of a dance or a tune
senses.definitionCN: 动作或曲调快速而有弹跳感
senses.example: The band played a frisky little tune.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队奏了一支轻快的小曲。
senses.why: Fast, hopping movement gives the word a musical, rhythmic sense.
senses.whyCN: 快速、跳跃的动作给这个词带来音乐般的节奏义。

senses.title: Cheerfully restless
senses.definition: too full of energy to stay still or calm
senses.definitionCN: 精力过盛，难以安坐或平静
senses.example: The children grew frisky as the rain kept them indoors.
senses.exampleCN: 雨把孩子们困在屋里，他们越来越坐不住。
senses.why: When energy has nowhere to go, playfulness turns into restlessness.
senses.whyCN: 能量无处释放时，爱闹就变成了坐立不安。

intro.en: Frisky comes from frisk, a verb of lively jumping; frisk is generally traced through Old French frisque to Middle Dutch frisch, fresh or lively.
intro.cn: frisky 来自表示欢快蹦跳的动词 frisk，一般认为 frisk 经古法语 frisque 追溯到中古荷兰语 frisch（新鲜的、活泼的）。

items.en: Frisch means fresh, new, and lively, and is related to English fresh.
items.cn: frisch 意为新鲜的、新的、活泼的，与英语 fresh 同源。

items.en: Frisque means lively, brisk, and merry.
items.cn: frisque 意为活泼的、轻快的、欢快的。

items.en: The verb frisk enters English with the sense of jumping about.
items.cn: 动词 frisk 以「到处蹦跳」之义进入英语。

items.en: The adjective frisky is formed from frisk plus -y.
items.cn: 形容词 frisky 由 frisk 加 -y 构成。

items.en: Frisky keeps the playful sense and often describes young animals.
items.cn: 现代英语的 frisky 保留戏耍义，常用来形容幼小的动物。

note.en: Frisky sits inside the frisk family and beside the wider set of playful and lively words.
note.cn: frisky 位于 frisk 词族之内，也与「顽皮」「活泼」的更大词场相邻。

entries.definition: to jump about playfully
in a playful and lively way
playful energy
full of fun
full of energy
easily excited and jumpy

normalIntro.en: Frisky is frisk plus -y: the suffix turns a jumping verb into a jumping adjective.
normalIntro.cn: frisky 是 frisk 加 -y：词尾把「蹦跳」的动词变成「爱蹦跳」的形容词。

normal.en: Frisk means to jump about, and frisky describes whoever keeps doing it.
normal.cn: frisk 意为蹦来蹦去，frisky 就形容老是这样跳的人或动物。

normal.en: A frisky puppy runs in circles for no reason at all.
normal.cn: a frisky puppy 会无缘无故地绕圈跑。

normal.en: Frisky behaviour is playful, not serious.
normal.cn: frisky behaviour 是嬉闹的，不是正经的。

normal.en: Friskier and friskiest compare rising levels of playfulness.
normal.cn: friskier 与 friskiest 比较顽皮程度的高低。

normal.en: The same root gives English fresh, so frisky carries a hint of new energy.
normal.cn: 同一词根还给出英语 fresh，所以 frisky 带一点「新鲜劲儿」。

abstract.en: Picture a puppy spinning in circles until it falls over.
abstract.cn: 想象一只小狗转圈转到自己跌倒。

abstract.en: See a hand tapping a glass and a wink across the table.
abstract.cn: 想象桌边有人敲着杯子、递来一个眼色。

abstract.en: Hear a fiddle tune that makes the dancers hop.
abstract.cn: 听一段让舞者跟着蹦跳的提琴曲。

examples.en: The frisky lambs raced across the field.
examples.cn: 欢蹦乱跳的小羊在田野上奔跑。

examples.en: A frisky mood kept the whole party laughing.
examples.cn: 欢闹的情绪让整个聚会笑声不断。

examples.en: The music grew friskier as the night went on.
examples.cn: 夜色渐深，音乐也越发轻快。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗里斯奇」——听上去像「free sky」，联想在开阔的天空下撒欢；这只是谐音联想，并非词源。

root: 中古荷兰语 frisch（新鲜的、活泼的）→ 古法语 frisque（轻快的）→ 英语 frisk（蹦跳）→ frisk 加 -y → frisky，核心义「蹦跳不停」。

sensesIntro.en: Frisky first means playful energy in action, then a light flirtatious manner, then brisk rhythm, and finally restless energy.
sensesIntro.cn: frisky 先指动作里的顽皮精力，再指轻佻的态度，继而指轻快的节奏，最后指无处释放的躁动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a puppy circling a pair of ankles, tail blurred with speed.
core.cn: 核心意象：小狗绕着人的脚边打转，尾巴快得看不清。

branches.en: Jumping play is the base sense.
branches.cn: 蹦跳玩耍是基础义项。

branches.en: Playful energy aimed at a person becomes flirtation.
branches.cn: 顽皮精力指向他人就变成调情。

branches.en: The same energy set to a beat becomes springy rhythm.
branches.cn: 同样的精力配上节拍就成了轻快节奏。

branches.en: Energy with no outlet turns into restlessness.
branches.cn: 精力无处释放就转为躁动。

branches.en: Both the happy romping and the restless fidgeting come from too much energy.
branches.cn: 欢闹与坐不住都来自过剩的精力。

intro.en: Frisky is an English adjective built from frisk and -y, with friskiness and friskily completing the family.
intro.cn: frisky 是由 frisk 与 -y 构成的英语形容词，friskiness 与 friskily 补全这个词族。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin ancestor: the line runs through Old French frisque back to Middle Dutch frisch, so no Latin cognates are recorded here.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁语祖形，线索经古法语 frisque 回到中古荷兰语 frisch，因此这里不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: Frisch is the probable source of the French form.
items.exampleCN: frisch 可能是法语形式的来源。

items.example: Frisque passes into English as frisk.
items.exampleCN: frisque 进入英语成为 frisk。

items.example: Lambs frisk in the spring fields.
items.exampleCN: 羊羔在春天的田野里蹦跳。

items.example: The noun keeps the idea of a quick romp.
items.exampleCN: 名词保留「一阵欢跳」的意思。

items.meaningCN: 充满……的；倾向于……的形容词词尾
items.example: The suffix -y forms frisky from frisk.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 由 frisk 构成 frisky。

items.example: Frisky describes young animals at play.
items.exampleCN: frisky 形容玩耍中的幼小动物。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ness forms friskiness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 friskiness。

items.example: The suffix -ily forms friskily.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ily 构成 friskily。

items.example: Friskiness names the quality of being frisky.
items.exampleCN: friskiness 表示 frisky 的性质。

definition_zh: 连衣裙；女式长裙；僧袍；罩衫
definition_en: a dress for a woman or a girl, or a long loose garment worn by a monk
core_image: 一件挂在木衣架上的布裙，裙摆垂到脚踝
scene: 旧衣店里，一件碎花布裙挂在木架上，裙摆垂到脚踝。A faded cotton frock hung on the rail, its hem brushing the floor.
sceneCN: 这里 frock 是「连衣裙」（第 1 个义项：女式连衣裙）；句意：衣架上挂着一件褪色的棉布连衣裙，裙摆擦着地面。

pos.zh: 连衣裙；女式长裙；僧袍；罩衫；男式长礼服

derivatives.zh: 由 de-（去除）加 frock（僧袍）构成，义为「解除神职」
由 un-（反向）加 frock（僧袍）构成，义为「免去神职」
由 frock 加 -ed 构成，义为「穿着长袍的」

senses.title: A dress for women
senses.definition: a dress worn by a woman or a girl, usually with a skirt
senses.definitionCN: 女性或女孩穿的连衣裙，通常带裙摆
senses.example: She wore a printed frock to the wedding.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿了一条印花连衣裙去参加婚礼。
senses.why: The word began as a loose outer garment and narrowed to a dress for women in the eighteenth century.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原指宽松的外袍，十八世纪缩小为女性连衣裙。

senses.title: A habit of a monk
senses.definition: a long loose garment worn by a monk
senses.definitionCN: 修士穿着的宽松长袍
senses.example: The monk folded his dark frock after the service.
senses.exampleCN: 仪式结束后，修士叠起了他的深色僧袍。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense, since Old French froc named the habit of a monk.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的义项，因为古法语 froc 就指僧袍。

senses.title: A work smock
senses.definition: a loose garment worn over other clothes while working
senses.definitionCN: 干活时罩在其他衣服外面的宽松外衣
senses.example: The painter put on a coarse frock before mixing colours.
senses.exampleCN: 画家在调色前套上一件粗布罩衫。
senses.why: Loose outer garments for work kept the general shape of the old froc.
senses.whyCN: 干活穿的宽松外衣保留了旧时 froc 的基本形制。

senses.title: A long coat for men
senses.definition: a knee-length coat worn by men in the past, now mainly in the phrase frock coat
senses.definitionCN: 旧时男子穿的及膝外套，今多用于 frock coat 一语
senses.example: The old photograph shows him in a black frock coat.
senses.exampleCN: 那张老照片里，他穿着黑色长礼服。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century tailoring borrowed the word for a formal long coat.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪的裁缝把这词借去指正式的长外套。

intro.en: Frock came into English from Old French froc, the habit of a monk, generally traced to Medieval Latin froccus and often linked to Latin floccus, a tuft of wool.
intro.cn: frock 由古法语 froc（僧袍）进入英语，一般认为源于中世纪拉丁语 froccus，常被认为与拉丁语 floccus（一簇羊毛）有关。

items.en: Froccus names a garment for a monk, though its own origin is debated.
items.cn: froccus 指修士的袍服，但它本身的来源仍有争议。

items.en: Floccus means a tuft of wool and is offered as a possible source, not a certain one.
items.cn: floccus 意为一簇羊毛，被认为是可能的来源，但并不确定。

items.en: Froc means the habit of a monk or a loose garment.
items.cn: froc 意为僧袍或宽松外衣。

items.en: English borrows the word for a loose outer garment.
items.cn: 英语借入该词，指宽松的外袍。

items.en: Frock narrows to the dress of a woman or girl.
items.cn: 十八世纪，frock 缩小为女式连衣裙。

items.en: Frock survives in British use for dresses and in the fixed phrase frock coat.
items.cn: 现代英语中 frock 仍见于英式「连衣裙」用法与固定说法 frock coat。

note.en: Frock is a garment word with a small family through defrock and unfrock, and it sits beside dress, gown, and smock.
note.cn: frock 是衣物词，经由 defrock 与 unfrock 形成一个很小的词族，并与 dress、gown、smock 相邻。

entries.definition: to remove a priest from office
to strip a priest of office
wearing a frock or long robe
a one-piece garment for a woman or girl
a long formal dress or robe
a loose work garment

normalIntro.en: Frock is a loose garment word, and its clearest trace today is the habit of a monk inside defrock.
normalIntro.cn: frock 是宽松外袍的词，今天最清楚的痕迹是 defrock 里那件僧袍。

normal.en: A frock is a dress, and a frock coat is a long coat for men.
normal.cn: frock 是连衣裙，而 frock coat 是男式长外套。

normal.en: To defrock a priest is to take away the frock and the office with it.
normal.cn: defrock 一位神父，就是拿走袍子连同职位。

normal.en: Cotton frocks are summer clothes, while woollen frocks suit colder days.
normal.cn: 棉布 frock 是夏装，羊毛 frock 适合更冷的日子。

normal.en: The frock of a monk is long, simple, and belted at the waist.
normal.cn: 僧袍又长又素，腰间系带。

normal.en: Compare dress: frock sounds older and more British.
normal.cn: 对比 dress：frock 听起来更旧派、更英式。

abstract.en: Picture a floral dress swinging on a wooden hanger.
abstract.cn: 想象一条碎花裙在木衣架上轻轻摆动。

abstract.en: See a hooded figure walking a cold cloister, robe dragging on stone.
abstract.cn: 想象一个戴兜帽的身影走在寒冷的回廊里，长袍拖过石板。

abstract.en: Imagine a painter rolling up wide sleeves before work.
abstract.cn: 想象画家开工前挽起宽大的袖子。

examples.en: She chose a simple blue frock for the party.
examples.cn: 她挑了一条素净的蓝裙子去参加聚会。

examples.en: The frock of the monk was grey and reached his ankles.
examples.cn: 那位修士的袍子是灰色的，长到脚踝。

examples.en: He had his portrait painted in a frock coat.
examples.cn: 他让人画了一幅穿长礼服的肖像。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗洛克」——谐音像一块布被「裹」住身体，就成了袍子；这只是谐音联想，并非词源。

root: 中世纪拉丁语 froccus（修士袍服，来源存疑，或与拉丁语 floccus「一簇羊毛」有关）→ 古法语 froc（僧袍）→ 英语 frock，核心义「宽松外袍」。

sensesIntro.en: Frock starts with the loose robe of a monk, widens to working outer garments, narrows to a dress for women, and survives in the long coat for men.
sensesIntro.cn: frock 从修士的宽松长袍开始，扩及干活穿的外衣，再缩小为女式连衣裙，并在男式 frock coat 中留存。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a loose cloth garment hanging from a wooden hanger, hem near the floor.
core.cn: 核心意象：一件宽松布袍挂在木衣架上，裙摆接近地面。

branches.en: The habit of a monk is the oldest recorded sense.
branches.cn: 僧袍是最早见于记录的义项。

branches.en: Work smocks kept the loose shape of the old robe.
branches.cn: 工作罩衫保留了旧袍的宽松形制。

branches.en: The dress for women is the modern everyday sense in British English.
branches.cn: 女式连衣裙是英式英语里现代的日常义项。

branches.en: The frock coat is a nineteenth-century menswear sense.
branches.cn: frock coat 是十九世纪男装的义项。

branches.en: Both the dress and the smock are single loose garments put on over the body.
branches.cn: 连衣裙与罩衫都是套在身上的单件宽松衣物。

intro.en: Frock is a borrowing with almost no English derivatives of its own; defrock and unfrock grew from the habit sense.
intro.cn: frock 是借词，自身几乎没有英语派生词；defrock 与 unfrock 是从僧袍义长出来的。

latinIntro.en: Medieval Latin froccus is the recorded Latin form, though its own origin is uncertain and a link to Latin floccus is only a suggestion.
latinIntro.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 froccus 是有记录的拉丁形式，但它本身的来源不确定，与拉丁语 floccus 的联系只是一种推测。

items.example: Froccus is the earliest recorded Latin form.
items.exampleCN: froccus 是最早记录的拉丁形式。

items.example: Floccus is sometimes proposed as the source.
items.exampleCN: floccus 有时被提出来作为来源。

items.meaning: habit of a monk, loose garment
items.example: Froc passes into English as frock.
items.exampleCN: froc 进入英语成为 frock。

items.example: Frock first names a loose robe.
items.exampleCN: frock 最初指宽松长袍。

items.example: The dress sense appears in the eighteenth century.
items.exampleCN: 连衣裙义在十八世纪出现。

items.example: The prefix de- forms defrock.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 de- 构成 defrock。

items.meaning: to remove a priest from office
items.example: Defrock literally means to take away the frock.
items.exampleCN: defrock 字面义是拿走那件袍子。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unfrock.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unfrock。

items.meaning: to strip a priest of office
items.example: Unfrock is a synonym of defrock.
items.exampleCN: unfrock 是 defrock 的同义词。

definition_zh: 爱嬉闹的；欢闹的；调皮捣蛋的
definition_en: full of playful fun and light-hearted mischief
core_image: 一群孩子追着球跑过草坪，笑声一路撒在后面
scene: 夏日的草坪上，几个孩子追着球跑，笑声一路撒在身后。The frolicsome children chased the ball across the lawn.
sceneCN: 这里 frolicsome 是「爱嬉闹的」（第 1 个义项：爱玩闹、欢快）；句意：那群嬉闹的孩子追着球跑过草坪。

pos.zh: 爱嬉闹的；欢闹的；调皮捣蛋的；欢快轻巧的

derivatives.zh: 由 frolicsome 加 -ness 构成，义为「嬉闹的性情」
frolicsome 的词干，义为「嬉戏；欢闹」
由 frolic 加 -ing 构成，义为「嬉闹」
由 frolic 加 -y 构成，义为「爱嬉戏的」

senses.title: Playfully merry
senses.definition: full of light-hearted fun and playful energy
senses.definitionCN: 充满轻松愉快、爱玩闹的劲头
senses.example: The frolicsome crowd danced until midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 那群嬉闹的人一直跳到半夜。
senses.why: Frolic names merry play, and the suffix -some adds the idea of being full of it.
senses.whyCN: frolic 指欢快的游戏，词尾 -some 加上「充满……」的意思。

senses.title: Lively in romping play
senses.definition: running and jumping about in play, especially of young animals
senses.definitionCN: 在玩耍中跑跳不停，尤指幼小动物
senses.example: A frolicsome lamb kicked up its heels in the yard.
senses.exampleCN: 一只撒欢的羊羔在院子里尥起了蹶子。
senses.why: The word often describes animals at play, where the fun shows as jumping.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常用来描写玩耍中的动物，欢乐直接表现为蹦跳。

senses.title: Cheerfully mischievous
senses.definition: playfully naughty in a way that is not serious
senses.definitionCN: 顽皮地不听话，但并不严重
senses.example: A frolicsome wink told me the trick was planned.
senses.exampleCN: 一个调皮的眼色告诉我，这个恶作剧是事先安排好的。
senses.why: Merry energy aimed at other people becomes harmless mischief.
senses.whyCN: 欢快的精力指向他人，就变成无害的恶作剧。

senses.title: Light-hearted in tone
senses.definition: cheerful and light in mood, as of music or an occasion
senses.definitionCN: 气氛或音乐欢快轻盈
senses.example: The frolicsome tune suited the summer fair.
senses.exampleCN: 那支欢快的曲子正适合夏季集市。
senses.why: Playful movement translates into a light rhythm in music and festivity.
senses.whyCN: 嬉闹的动作转到音乐与节庆里，就成了轻快的节奏。

intro.en: Frolicsome is frolic plus the suffix -some, meaning full of; frolic is generally traced to Middle Dutch vrolijk, merry.
intro.cn: frolicsome 是 frolic 加词尾 -some（充满……的）；frolic 一般认为来自中古荷兰语 vrolijk（欢快的）。

items.en: Frō means merry or gay.
items.cn: frō 意为欢快的、愉快的。

items.en: Vrolik means cheerful and merry, built with a suffix meaning like.
items.cn: vrolik 意为欢快的，由表示「像……」的后缀构成。

items.en: Vrolijk carries the same merry sense into Dutch.
items.cn: vrolijk 把同样的欢快义带入荷兰语。

items.en: Frolic enters English as a word for merry play.
items.cn: 十六世纪 frolic 以「欢快的游戏」之义进入英语。

items.en: The suffix -some forms frolicsome, meaning full of merry play.
items.cn: 词尾 -some 构成 frolicsome，意为充满欢闹。

items.en: Frolicsome stays slightly literary and often describes children and young animals.
items.cn: 现代英语的 frolicsome 略带书面色彩，常形容孩子与幼小动物。

note.en: Frolicsome is the adjective of the frolic family and sits beside playful, merry, and mischievous words.
note.cn: frolicsome 是 frolic 词族的形容词，与「顽皮」「欢快」「调皮」诸词相邻。

entries.definition: merry play
lively play
playful merriness
full of fun
cheerful and lively
playfully naughty

normalIntro.en: Frolicsome is frolic plus -some: the suffix says the person is made of merry play.
normalIntro.cn: frolicsome 是 frolic 加 -some：这个词尾说明此人「满身都是欢闹」。

normal.en: Frolic is merry play, and frolicsome means full of it.
normal.cn: frolic 是欢快的游戏，frolicsome 意为充满这种游戏。

normal.en: The suffix -some, as in handsome, adds the idea of a strong quality.
normal.cn: 词尾 -some 如同在 handsome 中那样，表示某种性质很强。

normal.en: Frolicsome children rarely sit still for long.
normal.cn: frolicsome 的孩子很少长时间安静坐着。

normal.en: A frolicsome tune lifts the mood of a room.
normal.cn: 一支 frolicsome 的曲子能提亮一屋子的气氛。

normal.en: Frolicking and frolicsome share the same playful root.
normal.cn: frolicking 与 frolicsome 共享同一个嬉戏词根。

abstract.en: See a ring of children running across a lawn with a ball.
abstract.cn: 想象一圈孩子在草坪上追着一个球跑。

abstract.en: Picture a lamb kicking both back legs at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一只羊羔同时尥起两条后腿。

abstract.en: Imagine a face with one eyebrow raised and a finger on the lips.
abstract.cn: 想象一张脸挑起眉毛、把手指按在嘴边。

examples.en: The frolicsome crowd filled the square with laughter.
examples.cn: 欢闹的人群让广场充满笑声。

examples.en: Frolicsome puppies tumbled over each other on the grass.
examples.cn: 撒欢的小狗们在草地上互相翻滚。

examples.en: Her frolicsome mood made even the long wait seem short.
examples.cn: 她欢闹的心情让漫长的等待也显得短暂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗罗利克萨姆」——里面藏着「frolic」（嬉戏），像一群人笑闹着滚成一团；这只是谐音联想，并非词源。

root: 古撒克逊语 frō（欢快的）加中古低地德语 -lik（像……的）→ vrolik → 中古荷兰语 vrolijk（欢快的）→ 英语 frolic（嬉戏）加 -some → frolicsome，核心义「满身欢闹」。

sensesIntro.en: Frolicsome begins with merry play, moves to the romping play of animals, then to harmless mischief, and finally to a light tone in music.
sensesIntro.cn: frolicsome 从欢快的游戏开始，转到动物撒欢，再到无害的调皮，最后到音乐上的轻快格调。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: children and a ball crossing a lawn, laughter trailing behind them.
core.cn: 核心意象：孩子和一只球跑过草坪，笑声在身后拖成一条线。

branches.en: Merry play is the base sense of the adjective.
branches.cn: 欢闹的游戏是这个形容词的基础义。

branches.en: Animal play makes the fun visible as jumping.
branches.cn: 动物玩耍让欢乐表现为蹦跳。

branches.en: Playfulness aimed at people becomes mischief.
branches.cn: 顽皮指向他人就成了恶作剧。

branches.en: The same lightness transfers to music and festivity.
branches.cn: 同样的轻盈转到音乐与节庆上。

branches.en: Romping and mischief are both play with no serious aim.
branches.cn: 撒欢与恶作剧都是没有正经目的的游戏。

intro.en: Frolicsome is frolic plus -some, and the family also holds frolicking and frolicsomeness.
intro.cn: frolicsome 是 frolic 加 -some，其词族还有 frolicking 与 frolicsomeness。

latinIntro.en: No Latin word lies behind this adjective; the line runs from Old Saxon frō through Middle Dutch vrolijk, so no Latin cognates are recorded here.
latinIntro.cn: 这个形容词背后没有拉丁词：线索从古撒克逊语 frō 经中古荷兰语 vrolijk 而来，因此这里不列拉丁同源词。

items.example: Frō is the oldest traced element of the family.
items.exampleCN: frō 是这个词族可追溯的最早成分。

items.example: The suffix -līk builds the sense merry-like.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -līk 构成「像欢快那样的」意思。

items.example: Vrolik spreads the word into the Low German area.
items.exampleCN: vrolik 把这个词扩展到低地德语地区。

items.example: Vrolijk is the form English borrowed.
items.exampleCN: vrolijk 是英语借入的形式。

items.example: Frolic names the play itself.
items.exampleCN: frolic 指嬉戏本身。

items.example: The verb frolic keeps the same fun.
items.exampleCN: 动词 frolic 保留同样的乐趣。

items.example: The suffix -some forms frolicsome.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -some 构成 frolicsome。

items.example: Frolicsome describes children at play.
items.exampleCN: frolicsome 形容玩耍中的孩子。

items.example: Frolicsomeness names the quality.
items.exampleCN: frolicsomeness 表示这种性质。

definition_zh: 前面的；正面的；前额的；额叶的；锋面的
definition_en: relating to the front of something or to the forehead
core_image: 一张正对着你的脸，额头先迎上来
scene: 医生把片子举到灯下，指着额头的位置。The scan showed a small crack in the frontal bone.
sceneCN: 这里 frontal 是「前额的」（第 2 个义项：与额头有关）；句意：片子显示额骨上有一道小裂口。

pos.zh: 前面的；正面的；前额的；额叶的；锋面的
额骨；祭坛前饰布

derivatives.zh: 正面地；在前部（frontal 加副词后缀 -ly）
前额叶的（pre- 前 + frontal 额叶的）
前面；正面（与 frontal 同出 frons 词干）

senses.title: At the front
senses.definition: placed at or belonging to the front of something
senses.definitionCN: 位于某物前部或属于前部的
senses.example: The frontal panel of the machine carries the main switches.
senses.exampleCN: 机器的前面板装着主要开关。
senses.why: Latin frons means both forehead and front, so the adjective first marks whatever sits at the front.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 frons 兼指额头与正面，所以这个词最先标记位于前面的东西。

senses.title: Of the forehead
senses.definition: relating to the forehead or the brow
senses.definitionCN: 与额头或眉部有关的
senses.example: A frontal headache usually starts behind the brow.
senses.exampleCN: 前额痛通常从眉后开始。
senses.why: The same Latin noun names the forehead, so the adjective keeps that anatomical sense beside the spatial one.
senses.whyCN: 同一个拉丁名词也指额头，所以这个词在空间义之外保留了这一身体部位义。

senses.title: Of the brain lobe
senses.definition: relating to the front part of the brain
senses.definitionCN: 与大脑前部有关的
senses.example: Damage to the frontal lobe can change how a person behaves.
senses.exampleCN: 额叶受损会改变一个人的行为方式。
senses.why: The brain area lying at the front of the skull simply took the adjective of the front.
senses.whyCN: 位于颅骨前部的脑区直接沿用了表示「前部」的形容词。

senses.title: Of a weather front
senses.definition: relating to the boundary where two air masses meet
senses.definitionCN: 与两股气团交汇的边界有关的
senses.example: Frontal rain falls when warm air rides up over cold air.
senses.exampleCN: 暖空气爬到冷空气之上时就形成锋面雨。
senses.why: Meteorology borrowed the word for the leading edge of an air mass, which is its front.
senses.whyCN: 气象学借用了这个词，指气团的前缘，也就是它的「正面」。

senses.title: Direct and open
senses.definition: direct, met face to face instead of being avoided
senses.definitionCN: 直接的、面对面而不回避的
senses.example: They launched a frontal assault on the new policy.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对新政策发起了正面抨击。
senses.why: Something frontal meets you face to face, so the word also means an open, unhidden approach.
senses.whyCN: frontal 的东西与你面对面相遇，所以这个词也指公开、不遮掩的做法。

senses.title: Facing the viewer
senses.definition: shown facing the viewer, as in painting or photography
senses.definitionCN: 在绘画或摄影中正对观者展示的
senses.example: The portrait is a frontal view of the seated queen.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画像呈现的是坐着的女王正面像。
senses.why: A figure painted head on presents its front to us, so art writing calls the pose frontal.
senses.whyCN: 画中人物正对观者，就是把正面呈现给我们，所以艺术写作称这种姿态为 frontal。

senses.title: The forehead bone
senses.definition: the bone that forms the forehead
senses.definitionCN: 构成前额的骨块
senses.example: The frontal is one of the flat bones of the skull.
senses.exampleCN: 额骨是颅骨的扁平骨之一。
senses.why: Latin frontalis was used as a noun for the bone of the brow, and English kept that short noun.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 frontalis 曾被用作名词指眉骨，英语保留了这个简短的名词用法。

senses.title: An altar frontal
senses.definition: a cloth or panel covering the front of an altar
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖祭坛正面的布或饰板
senses.example: The embroidered frontal changes with the church season.
senses.exampleCN: 绣花祭坛前饰布随教会节期更换。
senses.why: The front of an altar is its frontal, so the cloth hung there took the same name.
senses.whyCN: 祭坛的正面就是它的 frontal，挂在那里的布便得了同一个名字。

intro.en: Frontal comes from Latin frontalis, an adjective from frons, the forehead or the front of a thing.
intro.cn: frontal 来自拉丁语 frontalis，是 frons（额头、某物的正面）的形容词形式。

items.en: Frons, with the stem front-, means the forehead and also the front of a thing.
items.cn: frons（词干 front-）意为额头，也指某物的正面。

items.en: Frontalis is the adjective meaning of the forehead.
items.cn: frontalis 是意为「前额的」的形容词。

items.en: English borrows frontal as an anatomical adjective.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 frontal，用作解剖学形容词。

items.en: Frontal also names the cloth hung on the front of an altar.
items.cn: frontal 又用来指挂在祭坛正面的饰布。

items.en: Modern usage adds weather fronts, brain lobes, and direct attacks.
items.cn: 现代用法又加入了锋面、脑叶与正面进攻。

note.en: Frontal belongs to the frons family, and it also sits near the plain words for front.
note.cn: frontal 属于 frons 词族，也与表示「前面」的普通词相邻。

entries.definition: the forward part or side of something
entries.definitionCN: 前面；正面（与 frons 同源）

entries.definition: to face someone or something directly
entries.definitionCN: 直面；对抗（com- 加 frons，本义「面对面」）

entries.definition: bold and rude behaviour that shows no shame
entries.definitionCN: 厚颜无耻（由 ex- 加 frons 构成，本义「不要脸面」）

entries.definition: placed at or near the front
most forward in position
directed towards the front

normalIntro.en: Frontal is the adjective of the forehead and of the front, so it always points at what faces you.
normalIntro.cn: frontal 是「额头」与「正面」的形容词，总是指向正对着你的那一面。

normal.en: The Latin stem front- gives front, frontal, and confront.
normal.cn: 拉丁词干 front- 生出 front、frontal 与 confront。

normal.en: A frontal attack is one that you do not hide from.
normal.cn: frontal attack 就是你毫不回避的正面进攻。

normal.en: The frontal lobe sits at the front of the brain.
normal.cn: frontal lobe 位于大脑前部。

normal.en: The frontal bone is the bone of the brow.
normal.cn: frontal bone 就是眉骨所在的额骨。

normal.en: A frontal system brings rain along the edge of an air mass.
normal.cn: frontal system 沿着气团边缘带来降雨。

abstract.en: Picture a face turning towards you until the brow fills the frame.
abstract.cn: 想象一张脸转向你，直到额头占满画面。

abstract.en: Imagine touching the flat bone just above your eyes.
abstract.cn: 想象摸一摸眼睛上方那块平坦的骨头。

abstract.en: Think of a weather map where two air masses meet head on.
abstract.cn: 想象一张天气图，两股气团正面相遇。

examples.en: The frontal panel of the machine holds the switches.
examples.cn: 机器的前面板装着开关。

examples.en: He suffered a frontal injury just above the left eye.
examples.cn: 他左眼上方受了额部损伤。

examples.en: Cold frontal rain soaked the whole valley.
examples.cn: 冷锋降雨浸透了整个山谷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗朗头」——额头朝前；front 是前面，加 -al 变成形容词，记住「前面那块额头」。这只是拆词联想，不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 frons（额头、正面，词干 front-）→ 拉丁语 frontalis（前额的）→ 英语 frontal，核心义「正对前方的额头」。

sensesIntro.en: Frontal starts at the front of a thing, passes to the forehead and the brain lobe behind it, then extends to weather fronts, direct attacks, and the cloth on an altar front.
sensesIntro.cn: frontal 从「某物的正面」出发，转到额头与其后的脑叶，再延伸到锋面、正面进攻与祭坛前饰布。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face turned towards you, brow first.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张转向你的脸，额头先到。

branches.en: The plain front sense is the base of the adjective.
branches.cn: 单纯的「前面」义是这个词的底座。

branches.en: The forehead sense and the bone named after it belong together.
branches.cn: 额头的义项与以之命名的额骨属于一组。

branches.en: The brain lobe at the front borrowed the same adjective.
branches.cn: 位于前部的脑叶沿用了同一个形容词。

branches.en: A weather front is the leading edge of an air mass.
branches.cn: 锋面就是气团的前缘。

branches.en: Facing forward becomes directness in speech and a head-on pose in art.
branches.cn: 正面朝向在言语里变成直接，在绘画里变成正面像。

intro.en: Frontal is built on the Latin stem front-, with English front, confront, effrontery, and prefrontal around it.
intro.cn: frontal 建在拉丁词干 front- 上，周围有 front、confront、effrontery 与 prefrontal。

latinIntro.en: Latin frons means the forehead and the front, and frontalis is its adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 frons 意为额头和正面，frontalis 是它的形容词。

items.example: Frons is the source noun of the family.
items.exampleCN: frons 是这个词族的源头名词。

items.example: The stem front- appears inside frontalis.
items.exampleCN: 词干 front- 出现在 frontalis 里面。

items.example: The suffix -alis forms frontalis.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -alis 构成 frontalis。

items.example: Frontalis passes straight into English.
items.exampleCN: frontalis 直接进入英语。

items.example: The suffix -al shapes frontal.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 构成 frontal。

items.meaning: of the front or the forehead
items.example: Frontal keeps both Latin senses.
items.exampleCN: frontal 保留拉丁语的两个意思。

items.example: Front is the plain noun of the family.
items.exampleCN: front 是这个词族里最普通的名词。

items.example: Confront joins com- with frons.
items.exampleCN: confront 由 com- 与 frons 组合而成。

items.meaning: in front of the frontal lobe
items.example: Prefrontal adds the prefix pre-.
items.exampleCN: prefrontal 加上前缀 pre-。

definition_zh: 结果实；结实过程；果实器官；成果；实现
definition_en: the process of producing fruit, or the result that such a process brings
core_image: 枝头的青果一点点鼓起来，把花托撑成饱满的果实
scene: 果园里花瓣刚落，枝条上冒出绿色的小果。After the petals fell, fructification began on every branch.
sceneCN: 这里 fructification 是「结果实的过程」（第 1 个义项：植物结出果实）；句意：花瓣落后，每根枝条都开始结果。

pos.zh: 结果实；结实过程；果实器官；成果；实现

derivatives.zh: 结果实；使多产（fructus 果实 + -fy 使……）
结果实的；产果的（fructus + -ferous 带有……的）
多产的；有成果的（fructus 加 -ous）

senses.title: Bearing fruit
senses.definition: the process by which a plant produces fruit
senses.definitionCN: 植物结出果实的过程
senses.example: Fructification follows flowering in most orchard trees.
senses.exampleCN: 多数果树在开花之后结果。
senses.why: Latin fructus means fruit and the suffix marks a process, so the word names fruit making itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 fructus 意为果实，后缀表示过程，所以这个词直接命名「制造果实」这件事。

senses.title: The fruiting state
senses.definition: the condition of being fruitful or heavy with fruit
senses.definitionCN: 处于多产、果实累累的状态
senses.example: A long warm summer brought the vines to full fructification.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长而温暖的夏天让葡萄藤进入盛果状态。
senses.why: The same noun can name not the act but the state of being full of fruit.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词也可以不指动作，而指「果实挂满枝头」的状态。

senses.title: Fertilization
senses.definition: the act of making something fertile, used mainly in older biology
senses.definitionCN: 使某物受孕或多产的行为，多见于旧时生物学
senses.example: The old text speaks of fructification by pollen.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的文献说到由花粉完成的授精。
senses.why: Fructify could also mean to make fruitful, so the noun once covered the making fertile.
senses.whyCN: fructify 也可表示「使多产」，因此这个名词一度涵盖「使之受孕」。

senses.title: Fruit-bearing organs
senses.definition: the parts of a plant that bear fruit or spores, taken together
senses.definitionCN: 植物上结果或产孢的器官的总称
senses.example: Botanists once described the stamens as organs of fructification.
senses.exampleCN: 植物学家曾把雄蕊描述为结实器官。
senses.why: The word shifted from the process to the structures that carry the process out.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从「过程」转指执行该过程的结构。

senses.title: A fungal fruiting body
senses.definition: in mycology, the spore-producing structure of a fungus
senses.definitionCN: 真菌学中产生孢子的结构
senses.example: The white fructification on the log is a fungal fruiting body.
senses.exampleCN: 木头上的白色子实体是一种真菌的产孢结构。
senses.why: A mushroom is where a fungus bears its spores, so the fruit word moved into mycology.
senses.whyCN: 蘑菇是真菌「结果」产孢的地方，于是这个「果实」词进入了真菌学。

senses.title: A result or product
senses.definition: the result that an effort or an idea produces
senses.definitionCN: 努力或想法产生的结果
senses.example: The book was the fructification of ten years of notes.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书是十年笔记的结晶。
senses.why: Fruit is the end product of a plant, so the noun easily stands for the outcome of any work.
senses.whyCN: 果实是植物的最终产物，于是这个词很容易指任何工作的成果。

senses.title: Fulfilment
senses.definition: the carrying out or completion of a plan or hope
senses.definitionCN: 计划或希望的落实与完成
senses.example: The opening of the school was the fructification of a long campaign.
senses.exampleCN: 学校的落成是一场长期运动的实现。
senses.why: When a plan bears fruit it is completed, so fructification can name fulfilment.
senses.whyCN: 计划「结果」就意味着完成，所以这个词也能指「实现」。

senses.title: The fruiting season
senses.definition: the period of the year when a plant bears fruit
senses.definitionCN: 植物结果的那段时间
senses.example: In late summer the orchard reaches its fructification.
senses.exampleCN: 夏末时分，果园进入结实期。
senses.why: The process has a season, and the noun took on that stretch of time as well.
senses.whyCN: 这个过程有固定的时节，名词也就顺带指那段时间。

intro.en: Fructification comes from Latin fructificatio, built from fructus, fruit, and facere, to make.
intro.cn: fructification 来自拉丁语 fructificatio，由 fructus（果实）与 facere（做）构成。

items.en: Fructus means fruit and also enjoyment or profit.
items.cn: fructus 意为果实，也指享用或收益。

items.en: Facere means to make or to do.
items.cn: facere 意为制作、做。

items.en: Fructificare means to bear fruit or to make fruitful.
items.cn: fructificare 意为结果实或使多产。

items.en: Fructificatio names a bearing of fruit.
items.cn: fructificatio 指结果实这件事。

items.en: English takes fructification from Latin for botanical writing.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪从拉丁语借入这个词，用于植物学写作。

items.en: Modern English adds the figurative senses of result and fulfilment.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了「成果」与「实现」的比喻义。

note.en: Fructification is the noun of fruit making, close to fructify and to the ordinary words for results.
note.cn: fructification 是「造出果实」的名词，与 fructify 以及表示「成果」的普通词相邻。

entries.definition: to bear fruit or to make something fruitful
entries.definitionCN: 结果实；使多产（与 fructification 同出 fructus）

entries.definition: bearing fruit
productive or fruitful, now rather literary
entries.definitionCN: 多产的；有成果的（今多用于书面）

entries.definition: the achievement of something hoped for
the seed-bearing part of a plant
the gathering in of a crop

normalIntro.en: Fructification is fruit plus making: the -fic- part comes from the Latin verb for doing.
normalIntro.cn: fructification 是「果实」加「制作」：中间的 -fic- 来自拉丁语表示「做」的词。

normal.en: Fruct- is the Latin root for fruit, seen in fructify and fructose.
normal.cn: fruct- 是表示「果实」的拉丁词根，见于 fructify 与 fructose。

normal.en: The -fic- part comes from facere, to make, so the word means fruit making.
normal.cn: -fic- 来自 facere（做），所以这个词的意思就是「造出果实」。

normal.en: A fungus forms a fructification when it builds its spore-bearing body.
normal.cn: 真菌长出其产孢结构时，就是在形成 fructification。

normal.en: The process of fructification starts after pollination.
normal.cn: 结果实的过程在授粉之后开始。

normal.en: The fructification of an idea means the idea at last bears fruit.
normal.cn: 思想的 fructification 就是想法终于结出果实。

abstract.en: Watch a green fruit swell until the branch bends under it.
abstract.cn: 看着一颗青果鼓起来，直到枝条被压弯。

abstract.en: Picture a vine heavy with grapes at the end of summer.
abstract.cn: 想象夏末一串串葡萄把藤压得沉甸甸。

abstract.en: Imagine pollen grains landing and a seed starting to form.
abstract.cn: 想象花粉落下，种子开始成形。

examples.en: Fructification in the orchard begins a few weeks after the blossoms fall.
examples.cn: 果园里的结果过程在花落几周后开始。

examples.en: The fungus forms its fructification on the shaded side of the trunk.
examples.cn: 这种真菌在树干的背阴面形成子实体。

examples.en: Years of patient work reached fructification in one small discovery.
examples.cn: 多年的耐心工作在一项小发现中结出了成果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗鲁克提菲克」——念起来像果实「咔嚓」鼓起来；拆开看 fruct 是果实、fic 是做，合起来就是「做出果实」。谐音只是壳子，别当词源。

root: 拉丁语 fructus（果实、收益）+ facere（做）→ 拉丁语 fructificare（结果实）→ fructificatio（结果实的过程）→ 英语 fructification，核心义「把果实做出来」。

sensesIntro.en: Fructification runs from the act of bearing fruit through the fruiting state, the organs, and the fruiting body, and then opens into results, fulfilment, and the season itself.
sensesIntro.cn: fructification 从「结果实」这一动作出发，经过结果状态、结实器官与子实体，最后展开为成果、实现与结实季节。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a green fruit swelling on the branch until it is full.
core.cn: 核心意象：枝头的青果一直鼓到饱满。

branches.en: The process of bearing fruit is the base sense.
branches.cn: 结果实的过程是基础义项。

branches.en: The state and the season are the same process seen as a condition and as a time.
branches.cn: 状态义与季节义是同一过程分别被看作状况与时段。

branches.en: Making fertile and the organs that carry it out are the biological middle layer.
branches.cn: 授精与执行它的器官构成生物学的中间层。

branches.en: The fungal fruiting body is fruit bearing in another kingdom.
branches.cn: 真菌的子实体是另一个界里的「结果」。

branches.en: A result and its fulfilment are the fruit of work rather than of plants.
branches.cn: 成果与实现是工作的果实，而不是植物的果实。

intro.en: Fructification is a Latin compound of fruit and making, with fructify, fructiferous, and fructuous around it.
intro.cn: fructification 是「果实」与「制作」的拉丁语复合词，周围有 fructify、fructiferous 与 fructuous。

latinIntro.en: Latin fructus is fruit, facere is to make, and fructificatio is a bearing of fruit.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fructus 是果实，facere 是做，fructificatio 是结果实。

items.example: Fructus supplies the fruit half of the word.
items.exampleCN: fructus 提供这个词的「果实」一半。

items.example: Facere supplies the making half.
items.exampleCN: facere 提供「制作」那一半。

items.example: The root -fic- links fruit to making.
items.exampleCN: 词根 -fic- 把「果实」与「制作」连起来。

items.example: Fructificare is the Latin verb behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: fructificare 是这个名词背后的拉丁动词。

items.example: The suffix -ation turns the verb into a process noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 把动词变成表示过程的名词。

items.example: Fructify is the short English verb.
items.exampleCN: fructify 是简短的英语动词。

items.example: The suffix -ferous forms fructiferous.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ferous 构成 fructiferous。

items.example: Fructiferous describes a fruit-bearing plant.
items.exampleCN: fructiferous 描述会结果的植物。

items.example: Fructuous is the older adjective of fruitfulness.
items.exampleCN: fructuous 是表示「多产」的较老形容词。

items.example: Fructification keeps the botanical sense.
items.exampleCN: fructification 保留了植物学含义。

definition_zh: 履行；实现；完成；满足感；自我实现
definition_en: the act of completing something promised or hoped for, or the satisfaction it brings
core_image: 一只空杯被慢慢倒满，最后一滴水刚好落下
scene: 她把合同翻到最后一页，签下名字，把拖了半年的项目交了尾。The signature marked the fulfillment of a promise made two years before.
sceneCN: 这里 fulfillment 是「履行」（第 1 个义项：把承诺或义务做到）；句意：这个签名标志着两年前那个承诺得到了履行。

pos.zh: 履行；实现；完成；满足感；自我实现

derivatives.zh: 履行；实现（full 满 + fill 填）
令人满足的；有成就感的（fill 的现在分词作形容词）
感到满足的；已履行的（fill 的过去分词作形容词）

senses.title: Carrying out a duty
senses.definition: the act of doing what a promise, duty, or contract requires
senses.definitionCN: 把承诺、义务或合同要求做到的行为
senses.example: The fulfillment of the contract took three years.
senses.exampleCN: 合同的履行花了三年。
senses.why: The word joins full and fill, so a duty is fulfilled when it is filled up to the required line.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由 full（满）与 fill（填）合成，义务被填到规定的线，就是履行完毕。

senses.title: Making a wish real
senses.definition: the achievement of something hoped for or planned
senses.definitionCN: 希望或计划的事情得以达成
senses.example: The trip was the fulfillment of a childhood dream.
senses.exampleCN: 这次旅行实现了童年的梦想。
senses.why: A wish is like an empty vessel, and fulfillment fills it with the real thing.
senses.whyCN: 愿望像一个空容器，fulfillment 把真实的东西装进去。

senses.title: A feeling of satisfaction
senses.definition: a deep feeling that life or work has meaning and value
senses.definitionCN: 觉得生活或工作有意义、有价值的深切感受
senses.example: Teaching gives her a strong sense of fulfillment.
senses.exampleCN: 教书给她强烈的满足感。
senses.why: When what you do matches what you value, the filled vessel becomes a feeling, and the word names that feeling.
senses.whyCN: 当你所做的与你所看重的吻合，被填满的容器就变成一种感受，词也就指这种感受。

senses.title: Becoming fully oneself
senses.definition: the full development of personal abilities and character
senses.definitionCN: 个人能力与性格的充分发展
senses.example: He saw art as a path to personal fulfillment.
senses.exampleCN: 他把艺术看作通向自我实现的道路。
senses.why: Personal growth is filling the self to its full measure, which is why psychology made the word central.
senses.whyCN: 个人成长是把自我填到应有的分量，所以心理学把这个词放到了核心位置。

senses.title: A prophecy coming true
senses.definition: the realization of a prediction or a warning
senses.definitionCN: 预言或警告变成现实
senses.example: The flood was the fulfillment of the old warning.
senses.exampleCN: 那场洪水应验了古老的警告。
senses.why: A prediction is a hollow shape waiting to be filled by events, and its fulfillment is that filling.
senses.whyCN: 预言是一个等待事件来填充的空壳，它的实现就是被填满。

senses.title: Order processing
senses.definition: the work of picking, packing, and sending goods that customers have ordered
senses.definitionCN: 拣货、包装并把顾客订购的货物发出的工作
senses.example: The company moved its fulfillment to a larger warehouse.
senses.exampleCN: 公司把订单履行业务搬到了更大的仓库。
senses.why: A modern order is a promise to deliver, so the business sense keeps the old duty meaning.
senses.whyCN: 现代订单就是一份交付承诺，所以商业义仍保留旧的「尽责」含义。

senses.title: Satisfying a requirement
senses.definition: the meeting of a need, condition, or standard
senses.definitionCN: 需要、条件或标准得到满足
senses.example: The design ensures the fulfillment of safety standards.
senses.exampleCN: 该设计确保安全标准得到满足。
senses.why: A condition is a requirement with an empty slot, and fulfillment puts something into that slot.
senses.whyCN: 条件就是留有空位的要求，满足它就是把东西放进那个空位。

senses.title: The end of a term
senses.definition: the completion of a fixed period of time, as in an old legal phrase
senses.definitionCN: 固定期限走到尽头，多见于旧式法律表达
senses.example: At the fulfillment of the ten years, the lease ended.
senses.exampleCN: 十年期满之时，租约终止。
senses.why: When a set time is filled to its end, the period is fulfilled, and the noun names that ending.
senses.whyCN: 规定的时间被填到尽头，期限就届满，名词指这个终点。

intro.en: Fulfillment is a Germanic compound of full and fill, later given the noun suffix -ment.
intro.cn: fulfillment 是 full（满）与 fill（填）的日耳曼语复合词，后来加上名词后缀 -ment。

items.en: Fullfyllan means to fill up and so to complete.
items.cn: fullfyllan 意为填满，因而表示完成。

items.en: Full means full and fyllan means to fill.
items.cn: full 意为满，fyllan 意为填。

items.en: The verb appears as fulfilen and fulfille.
items.cn: 这个动词在中古英语中写作 fulfilen 与 fulfille。

items.en: The noun fulfillment adds -ment to the verb.
items.cn: 名词 fulfillment 在动词后加上 -ment。

items.en: Psychology gives the word its sense of personal satisfaction.
items.cn: 心理学赋予这个词「个人满足」的含义。

note.en: Fulfillment is the noun of filling something full, close to its verb family and to the words for satisfaction.
note.cn: fulfillment 是「把某物填满」的名词，与它的动词词族以及表示「满足」的词相邻。

entries.definition: to carry out a promise or duty
entries.definitionCN: 履行；实现（英式拼写，与 fulfillment 同一动词）

entries.definition: the British spelling of the same noun
entries.definitionCN: 同一名词的英式拼写（只是拼写不同，词义一致）

entries.definition: giving a feeling of satisfaction
entries.definitionCN: 令人满足的（动词加 -ing 构成的形容词）

entries.definition: the pleasure of having a need or wish met
something done successfully by effort
the act of finishing something

normalIntro.en: Fulfillment is full plus fill plus a noun ending: something is filled until nothing is missing.
normalIntro.cn: fulfillment 是「满」加「填」再加名词词尾：填到什么都不缺为止。

normal.en: Full plus fill: a promise is filled until nothing is left over.
normal.cn: full 加 fill：承诺被填到一点都不剩。

normal.en: The -ment suffix turns the verb fulfill into the name of the act.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ment 把动词 fulfill 变成表示行为的名词。

normal.en: Order fulfillment is the modern version of keeping a delivery promise.
normal.cn: order fulfillment 是「守住交付承诺」的现代版本。

normal.en: Self-fulfillment means filling your own potential to the top.
normal.cn: self-fulfillment 就是把自己的潜能填到顶。

normal.en: British writing drops one l and spells the noun fulfilment.
normal.cn: 英式写法少一个 l，拼作 fulfilment。

abstract.en: See a glass filled to the brim and set down without spilling.
abstract.cn: 看见一只杯子被倒到边缘，放下去时一滴不洒。

abstract.en: See a child finally reach the top of a climbing wall.
abstract.cn: 看见孩子终于爬到攀岩墙的顶端。

abstract.en: See a calm face after a long day of work well done.
abstract.cn: 看见一张在一天劳作之后平静的脸。

examples.en: The fulfillment of the contract took three years.
examples.cn: 合同的履行花了三年。

examples.en: She finds fulfillment in teaching children to read.
examples.cn: 她在教孩子读书中找到满足感。

examples.en: The warehouse handles fulfillment for the whole region.
examples.cn: 这个仓库负责整个区域的订单履行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「full（满）+ fill（填）+ ment（名词）」——把该做的填满，就是履行与实现。谐音「富尔菲门特」听着像「福气满门」，只是玩笑，不是词源。

root: 古英语 fullfyllan（full 满 + fyllan 填）→ 中古英语 fulfille → 英语 fulfill 加 -ment → fulfillment，核心义「把该做的填满、填到齐」。

sensesIntro.en: Fulfillment moves from filling a duty to filling a wish, then to the feeling of fullness, and finally to personal growth, fulfilled predictions, business orders, met standards, and an expired term.
sensesIntro.cn: fulfillment 从「填满义务」走到「填满愿望」，再到「被填满的感受」，最后延伸到个人成长、应验的预言、商业订单、被满足的标准与到期的期限。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a vessel filled to the brim, drop by drop.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只容器被一滴一滴地填到边缘。

branches.en: A duty and a standard are both filled to the line they set.
branches.cn: 义务与标准都是被填到各自规定的线。

branches.en: A wish and a prophecy are empty shapes that events fill.
branches.cn: 愿望与预言都是等待事件来填充的空壳。

branches.en: The feeling of fullness and the growth of the self are the inner side of the image.
branches.cn: 被填满的感受与自我的成长是这一意象的内在面。

branches.en: A business order is a promise that the warehouse fills.
branches.cn: 商业订单就是由仓库去填满的承诺。

branches.en: A fixed term is a container of time filled to its end.
branches.cn: 固定期限就是一只装时间、被填到尽头的容器。

intro.en: Fulfillment is Germanic rather than Latin: full and fill combine, and -ment names the result.
intro.cn: fulfillment 属日耳曼语源而非拉丁语源：full 与 fill 复合，-ment 命名结果。

latinIntro.en: Fulfillment has no Latin cognate, because it grew inside English from full and fill, so the Latin list is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: fulfillment 没有拉丁同族词，它是在英语内部由 full 与 fill 长成的，因此拉丁词条留空。

items.meaning: complete, holding as much as possible
items.example: Full supplies the first half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: full 提供这个复合词的前一半。

items.example: Fill supplies the action of the compound.
items.exampleCN: fill 提供这个复合词的动作。

items.meaning: result or state of an action
items.example: The suffix -ment turns fulfill into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ment 把 fulfill 变成名词。

items.meaning: to carry out a promise or duty
items.example: Fulfill is the base verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: fulfill 是这个词族的基础动词。

items.example: Fulfilling describes work that satisfies.
items.exampleCN: fulfilling 描述让人满足的工作。

items.example: Fulfilled describes a satisfied person.
items.exampleCN: fulfilled 描述一个感到满足的人。

items.meaning: the act of completing, or its satisfaction
items.example: Fulfillment keeps both the act and the feeling.
items.exampleCN: fulfillment 同时保留「行为」与「感受」。

items.meaningCN: 自我实现；自身潜能的发挥
items.example: Self-fulfillment adds the idea of the self.
items.exampleCN: self-fulfillment 加进了「自我」这一层。

definition_zh: 怒斥；猛烈抨击；爆炸；使爆炸；雷酸盐
definition_en: to protest violently, or to explode with a loud report
core_image: 一道闪电劈下，紧跟着一声炸雷与暴怒的吼叫
scene: 化学课上，老师把一小粒灰色粉末放在铁板上，用锤子轻轻一敲。The grain of mercury fulminate went off with a sharp crack.
sceneCN: 这里 fulminate 是「雷酸盐」（第 5 个义项：化学中的起爆药）；句意：那一小粒雷汞随着一声脆响爆炸了。

pos.zh: 怒斥；猛烈抨击；爆炸；雷鸣
使爆炸；引爆；厉声发出
雷酸盐；起爆药

derivatives.zh: 怒斥；猛烈抨击；爆响（fulminate 加 -ion）
轰响的；突然而猛烈的（用于疾病等，fulmin- 加 -ant）
雷酸的（化学用语，fulmin- 加 -ic）

senses.title: To denounce violently
senses.definition: to protest or condemn with loud and angry words
senses.definitionCN: 用响亮而愤怒的言辞抗议或谴责
senses.example: The minister fulminated against the new tax.
senses.exampleCN: 部长猛烈抨击这项新税。
senses.why: Latin fulmen is lightning, so angry speech is pictured as a bolt striking its target.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 fulmen 是闪电，于是愤怒的言辞被想象成击中目标的一道电光。

senses.title: To explode loudly
senses.definition: to explode with a sharp report, as certain chemicals do
senses.definitionCN: 像某些化学物质那样伴随脆响爆炸
senses.example: The dry powder fulminated when the hammer struck it.
senses.exampleCN: 锤子一敲，干燥的粉末就爆响了。
senses.why: A substance that flashes like lightning gave the verb its explosive sense.
senses.whyCN: 会像闪电一样闪爆的物质，赋予这个动词「爆炸」的义项。

senses.title: To set off an explosion
senses.definition: to cause a substance to explode
senses.definitionCN: 使某物质爆炸
senses.example: The charge was fulminated by a single spark.
senses.exampleCN: 一点火花就引爆了这枚装药。
senses.why: The verb works both ways: the substance fulminates and the spark fulminates it.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词可以两面用：物质自己爆响，火花使它爆响。

senses.title: To thunder
senses.definition: to make a sound like thunder, used in literary writing
senses.definitionCN: 发出雷一样的响声，多用于文学描写
senses.example: Organ music fulminated through the empty nave.
senses.exampleCN: 管风琴的乐声在空荡的中殿里轰响。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply thunder, the sound that gave the word all its force.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是打雷，正是这个声音给了这个词全部的力量。

senses.title: A fulminate salt
senses.definition: a salt of fulminic acid, used in detonators and fuses
senses.definitionCN: 雷酸的盐，用于雷管与引信
senses.example: Mercury fulminate is sensitive enough to fire on impact.
senses.exampleCN: 雷汞足够敏感，一撞就会起爆。
senses.why: Chemists named these explosive salts after the lightning they imitate.
senses.whyCN: 化学家把这些起爆盐命名为「闪电」，因为它们模仿闪电。

senses.title: To hurl out threats
senses.definition: to send forth threats or curses in a loud voice
senses.definitionCN: 用高声发出威胁或诅咒
senses.example: He fulminated curses at the gate.
senses.exampleCN: 他在门口厉声咒骂。
senses.why: A curse thrown out loud is another bolt of verbal lightning.
senses.whyCN: 高声抛出的诅咒，是又一道言语的闪电。

senses.title: To publish a papal bull
senses.definition: of a pope, to issue a bull or decree with formal censure
senses.definitionCN: 指教皇正式颁布诏书或带着谴责的敕令
senses.example: The pope fulminated a bull against the order.
senses.exampleCN: 教皇颁布诏书，谴责那个修会。
senses.why: A papal bull was published with thunderous authority, so the verb took that administrative sense.
senses.whyCN: 教皇诏书是以雷霆般的权威发布的，动词便承接了这一行政义。

senses.title: To flare up suddenly
senses.definition: to break out suddenly and fiercely, of anger or conflict
senses.definitionCN: 怒火或冲突突然而猛烈地爆发
senses.example: Anger fulminated in the crowded hall.
senses.exampleCN: 愤怒在拥挤的大厅里骤然爆发。
senses.why: Lightning does not gather slowly, and the word keeps that sudden flash.
senses.whyCN: 闪电不会慢慢聚集，这个词也保留了那种突然的闪击。

intro.en: Fulminate comes from Latin fulminare, to strike with lightning, from fulmen, lightning.
intro.cn: fulminate 来自拉丁语 fulminare（以闪电击打），源头是 fulmen（闪电）。

items.en: Fulmen means lightning and is the noun behind the whole family.
items.cn: fulmen 意为闪电，是整个词族背后的名词。

items.en: Fulminare means to flash or to strike with lightning.
items.cn: fulminare 意为闪电或以雷击打。

items.en: Fulminatio names a flashing of lightning.
items.cn: fulminatio 指闪电的闪击。

items.en: English fulminate first means to thunder and to denounce.
items.cn: 英语 fulminate 最初意为打雷与怒斥。

items.en: Chemistry names the explosive salts fulminates.
items.cn: 十九世纪的化学把起爆盐命名为 fulminate。

items.en: Modern use keeps the angry and the explosive senses side by side.
items.cn: 现代用法让「愤怒」与「爆炸」两个义项并行。

note.en: Fulminate is the lightning verb, with fulminant and fulmination in its family and thunder words nearby.
note.cn: fulminate 是「闪电」动词，词族里有 fulminant 与 fulmination，近旁则是「打雷」类词。

entries.definition: sudden and severe, as of a disease
entries.definitionCN: 突然而猛烈的（多形容疾病，与 fulmen 同源）

entries.definition: a loud denunciation or a blast
relating to fulminic acid
to make a loud rumbling sound
to burst with a loud noise
to condemn someone or something publicly

normalIntro.en: Fulminate carries Latin lightning inside it: whatever it does, it does with a flash and a bang.
normalIntro.cn: fulminate 里面装着拉丁语的「闪电」：无论做什么，都带着一道闪光和一声巨响。

normal.en: Fulmen is Latin for lightning, and -ate makes a verb.
normal.cn: fulmen 是拉丁语的闪电，-ate 把它变成动词。

normal.en: To fulminate against a plan is to attack it with thunderous words.
normal.cn: fulminate against a plan 就是用雷霆般的话攻击它。

normal.en: A fulminate is an explosive salt that goes off like a tiny thunderbolt.
normal.cn: fulminate 是一种起爆盐，爆炸时像一枚小雷。

normal.en: The adjective fulminant describes a disease that strikes like lightning.
normal.cn: 形容词 fulminant 形容像闪电一样突然袭来的疾病。

normal.en: Fulmination can be either a loud denunciation or a blast.
normal.cn: fulmination 既可以指高声怒斥，也可以指一次爆响。

abstract.en: See a storm cloud split and a white bolt hit a tower.
abstract.cn: 看见乌云裂开，一道白光击中对面的塔。

abstract.en: Hear the sharp crack that comes right after the flash.
abstract.cn: 听见闪光之后紧接着的那声脆响。

abstract.en: Watch a spark touch powder and the whole dish jump.
abstract.cn: 看见火花碰到粉末，整个盘子都跳起来。

examples.en: Critics fulminated against the plan for months.
examples.cn: 批评者们对这项计划猛烈抨击了好几个月。

examples.en: Mercury fulminate is handled with great care in a laboratory.
examples.cn: 实验室里取用雷汞要格外小心。

examples.en: He fulminated at the clerk who lost his file.
examples.cn: 他对着弄丢他档案的职员大声发火。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fulmen 闪电 + ate 动词」——像闪电一样劈下来：爆炸、雷鸣、怒斥。谐音「翻脸 mate」，一翻脸就开骂，只是联想，不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 fulmen（闪电，词干 fulmin-）→ 拉丁语 fulminare（打雷、雷击）→ fulminatio（闪击）→ 英语 fulminate，核心义「像闪电一样劈下」。

sensesIntro.en: Fulminate begins with lightning, so it covers thunder and explosion, then the salts that explode, and finally the angry speech that strikes like a bolt.
sensesIntro.cn: fulminate 从闪电出发，先涵盖雷鸣与爆炸，再指会爆炸的盐类，最后指像电光一样击出的愤怒言辞。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lightning bolt followed by a crack of thunder.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道闪电之后紧接一声炸雷。

branches.en: Angry speech and loud curses are verbal lightning.
branches.cn: 愤怒的言辞与高声咒骂是言语的闪电。

branches.en: The substance blasts and the spark blasts it.
branches.cn: 物质自己爆响，火花使它爆响。

branches.en: Thunder is the oldest sound sense of the word.
branches.cn: 雷鸣是这个词最古老的声音义项。

branches.en: The detonator salts are named after the lightning they copy.
branches.cn: 起爆盐类是以它们所模仿的闪电命名的。

branches.en: A published bull and a sudden flare of anger both arrive with authority.
branches.cn: 颁布的诏书与骤然爆发的怒火都以权威之势到来。

intro.en: Fulminate is built on Latin fulmen, lightning, with fulminant, fulmination, and fulminic around it.
intro.cn: fulminate 建在拉丁语 fulmen（闪电）上，周围有 fulminant、fulmination 与 fulminic。

latinIntro.en: Latin fulmen is lightning, fulminare is to strike with lightning, and fulminatio is a flashing.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fulmen 是闪电，fulminare 是以闪电击打，fulminatio 是闪击。

items.example: Fulmen is the noun at the centre of the family.
items.exampleCN: fulmen 是这个词族中心的名词。

items.example: The stem fulmin- carries the flash into English.
items.exampleCN: 词干 fulmin- 把那道闪光带进英语。

items.meaning: to flash, to strike with lightning
items.example: Fulminare is the direct verb source.
items.exampleCN: fulminare 是直接的动词来源。

items.example: The suffix -ate forms the English verb.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ate 构成英语动词。

items.example: Fulminatio supplies the noun pattern.
items.exampleCN: fulminatio 提供名词的构词模式。

items.example: Fulmination keeps the noun sense of a blast.
items.exampleCN: fulmination 保留「猛烈一击」的名词含义。

items.example: Fulminant describes a disease that strikes fast.
items.exampleCN: fulminant 形容迅速袭来的疾病。

items.example: Fulminic belongs to the chemistry of detonators.
items.exampleCN: fulminic 属于起爆药的化学用语。

items.example: Fulminate joins the lightning image to action.
items.exampleCN: fulminate 把闪电意象接到动作上。

definition_zh: 烟；有害气体；气味；怒气；发怒；冒烟
definition_en: smoke, gas, or vapour that rises from something, or the anger that seems to rise with it
core_image: 一缕刺鼻的灰烟从裂开的管子里升起
scene: 修车师傅掀开引擎盖，一股呛人的气味扑上来。A cloud of exhaust fumes rose from the broken pipe.
sceneCN: 这里 fume 是「废气」（第 8 个义项：引擎排出的气体）；句意：一股废气从破管子里升起来。

pos.zh: 烟；有害气体；气味；怒气
冒烟；散发气体；发怒；熏制

derivatives.zh: 烟雾弥漫的；带烟味的（fume 加 -y）
熏蒸；用烟熏消毒（fumus 加 -igare，同出「烟」的词根）
熏蒸；熏蒸消毒（fumigate 加 -ion）

senses.title: Smoke or vapour
senses.definition: smoke, gas, or vapour, especially when it is strong or harmful
senses.definitionCN: 烟、气体或蒸汽，尤指浓烈或有害的
senses.example: Thick fumes filled the basement after the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 火灾之后，浓烟灌满了地下室。
senses.why: Latin fumus is smoke, and the plural fumes covers any cloud of it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 fumus 是烟，复数 fumes 泛指任何一团这样的烟。

senses.title: An exhalation or odour
senses.definition: a smell or vapour that rises from a substance
senses.definitionCN: 从某物质升起的气味或蒸汽
senses.example: A sharp fume of vinegar came from the open jar.
senses.exampleCN: 打开的罐子里冒出一股刺鼻的醋味。
senses.why: Anything that rises like smoke can be called a fume, even when it is only a smell.
senses.whyCN: 凡是像烟一样往上升的东西都能叫 fume，哪怕它只是一种气味。

senses.title: A fit of anger
senses.definition: a short burst of anger, mainly in the phrase in a fume
senses.definitionCN: 一阵短暂的恼怒，主要用于 in a fume 这一说法
senses.example: She was in a fume over the lost tickets.
senses.exampleCN: 她为丢了的票气得直冒火。
senses.why: Anger was imagined as hot vapour rising inside the body, so it took the smoke word.
senses.whyCN: 愤怒被想象成体内升起的热气，于是借用了「烟」这个词。

senses.title: To emit smoke
senses.definition: to send out smoke, gas, or vapour
senses.definitionCN: 冒出烟、气体或蒸汽
senses.example: The old chimney fumed all winter.
senses.exampleCN: 那根老烟囱整个冬天都在冒烟。
senses.why: The noun became a verb for the act of putting smoke out.
senses.whyCN: 名词转成动词，表示把烟排放出来的动作。

senses.title: To show anger
senses.definition: to be very angry and to speak or write angrily
senses.definitionCN: 非常生气，并愤怒地说或写
senses.example: He fumed at the slow service.
senses.exampleCN: 他为服务太慢而发火。
senses.why: If anger is smoke, a person fuming is a person smoking with rage.
senses.whyCN: 如果愤怒是烟，那么 fuming 的人就是被怒火熏得冒烟的人。

senses.title: To smoke food or wood
senses.definition: to treat or colour something with smoke or vapour
senses.definitionCN: 用烟或蒸汽处理某物，或给它上色
senses.example: The hams were fumed over oak chips.
senses.exampleCN: 火腿在橡木屑上熏制。
senses.why: Treating goods with smoke is the old craft sense of the word.
senses.whyCN: 用烟处理货物，是这个词古老的技艺义。

senses.title: To vaporize
senses.definition: to pass off as vapour or to be given off as gas
senses.definitionCN: 以蒸汽形式散去，或被当作气体释放
senses.example: The acid fumed in the open air.
senses.exampleCN: 那种酸在敞开的空气里挥发。
senses.why: Smoke and vapour were not separated in the old word, so fume also means to vaporize.
senses.whyCN: 古词里烟与蒸汽不分，所以 fume 也能表示「挥发」。

senses.title: Exhaust gas
senses.definition: the gases that an engine or a machine sends out
senses.definitionCN: 引擎或机器排出的气体
senses.example: Bus fumes make the street hard to breathe in.
senses.exampleCN: 公交车的尾气让这条街很难呼吸。
senses.why: Modern engines produce a new kind of smoke, and the plural fumes names it.
senses.whyCN: 现代引擎制造出一种新的「烟」，复数的 fumes 就用来指它。

intro.en: Fume comes from Latin fumus, smoke, through Old French fum, and the anger sense grew in English.
intro.cn: fume 来自拉丁语 fumus（烟），经古法语 fum 传入英语，「怒气」义则是在英语里长出来的。

items.en: Fumus means smoke and vapour.
items.cn: fumus 意为烟与蒸汽。

items.en: Fumare means to smoke or to give off smoke.
items.cn: fumare 意为冒烟或放出烟气。

items.en: Fum carries the word into French as smoke.
items.cn: fum 以「烟」之义把这个词带进法语。

items.en: Fume appears in English for smoke and vapour.
items.cn: fume 出现在英语中，指烟与蒸汽。

items.en: The sense of a hot temper joins the smoke senses.
items.cn: 十六世纪，「火爆脾气」的义项加入了烟的各种含义。

items.en: Modern English adds exhaust fumes and chemical fumes.
items.cn: 现代英语又加入尾气与化学气体。

note.en: Fume is the smoke word of the fum- family, and it also sits near the plain words for smoke and steam.
note.cn: fume 是 fum- 词族里的「烟」词，也与表示烟与蒸汽的普通词相邻。

entries.definition: to disinfect something with smoke or fumes
entries.definitionCN: 用烟或气体熏蒸消毒（同出 fumus）

entries.definition: full of fumes or smoke
a pleasant-smelling liquid
entries.definitionCN: 香水（per- 加 fumare，本义「透过烟」）

entries.definition: the grey cloud rising from burning material
a gas-like cloud that rises from a liquid
the hot mist that rises from boiling water

normalIntro.en: Fume is Latin smoke, and the same word serves for the smoke of a chimney and the steam of a temper.
normalIntro.cn: fume 就是拉丁语的烟，同一个词既管烟囱里的烟，也管脾气冒出的「火气」。

normal.en: Latin fumus is smoke, and English fume is its short form.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 fumus 是烟，英语 fume 是它的简短形式。

normal.en: Exhaust fumes are the smoke of an engine.
normal.cn: exhaust fumes 就是引擎的「烟」。

normal.en: In a fume means boiling with anger, as if smoke were rising.
normal.cn: in a fume 表示怒气翻腾，好像有烟冒出来。

normal.en: To fume at someone is to speak while the anger smokes.
normal.cn: fume at someone 就是一边冒着怒火一边说话。

normal.en: Fumigate and perfume also grow from the same smoke root.
normal.cn: fumigate 与 perfume 也长在同一个「烟」词根上。

abstract.en: Watch a grey thread of smoke curl out of a cracked pipe.
abstract.cn: 看见一缕灰烟从裂开的管子里卷着上升。

abstract.en: Hold an open vinegar jar and let the sharp smell reach you.
abstract.cn: 拿着敞开的醋罐，让那股冲味扑到鼻子里。

abstract.en: See a kettle whistle and picture the steam as a temper.
abstract.cn: 看见水壶鸣叫，把那团蒸汽想成一股脾气。

examples.en: Exhaust fumes from the old bus made the street hard to breathe in.
examples.cn: 旧公交车的尾气让这条街很难呼吸。

examples.en: She was in a fume about the cancelled train.
examples.cn: 她为取消的列车气得直冒火。

examples.en: The chimney fumed for hours after the fire was lit.
examples.cn: 炉火点着后，烟囱冒了好几个小时的烟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「fume 烟」——谐音「浮烟」，烟往上浮；一肚子火也像烟一样往上冒，所以又指发怒。只是谐音联想，不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 fumus（烟）→ 拉丁语 fumare（冒烟）→ 古法语 fum → 中古英语 fume，核心义「向上飘的烟」。

sensesIntro.en: Fume starts as rising smoke, takes in smells and vapours, turns to the anger that rises like smoke, and ends with treated meat, vaporized acid, and engine exhaust.
sensesIntro.cn: fume 先是向上飘的烟，接着纳入气味与蒸汽，再转为像烟一样升起的怒气，最后落到熏制、挥发与引擎废气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin grey thread of smoke rising from a crack.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道细细的灰烟从裂缝里升起。

branches.en: Chimney smoke and engine exhaust are the same rising cloud.
branches.cn: 烟囱的烟与引擎的尾气是同一团上升的烟云。

branches.en: A smell rising from a jar and an acid vaporizing are both thin exhalations.
branches.cn: 罐子里升起的气味与挥发掉的酸都是稀薄的散发物。

branches.en: Hot vapour inside the body becomes the image of anger.
branches.cn: 体内的热气变成了怒气的意象。

branches.en: The plain verb simply says that smoke is coming out.
branches.cn: 最普通的动词义就是「有烟冒出来」。

branches.en: Smoke as a tool treats meat and wood.
branches.cn: 烟作为工具，用来处理肉与木材。

intro.en: Fume is built on the Latin smoke root fum-, with fumy, fumigate, fumigation, and perfume around it.
intro.cn: fume 建在拉丁语「烟」词根 fum- 上，周围有 fumy、fumigate、fumigation 与 perfume。

latinIntro.en: Latin fumus is smoke, fumare is to smoke, and fumigare is to smoke something out.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fumus 是烟，fumare 是冒烟，fumigare 是用烟熏某物。

items.example: Fumus is the noun at the centre of the family.
items.exampleCN: fumus 是这个词族中心的名词。

items.example: The stem fum- appears in fume and fumy.
items.exampleCN: 词干 fum- 出现在 fume 与 fumy 里。

items.example: Fumare is the direct verb source.
items.exampleCN: fumare 是直接的动词来源。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -y forms the adjective fumy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -y 构成形容词 fumy。

items.example: Fume keeps the plain smoke sense.
items.exampleCN: fume 保留最普通的「烟」义。

items.example: Fumy describes a smoky room.
items.exampleCN: fumy 形容烟雾弥漫的房间。

items.example: Fumigare adds the idea of using smoke as a tool.
items.exampleCN: fumigare 加进了「把烟当工具」的意思。

items.example: Fumigate grew from the Latin tool sense.
items.exampleCN: fumigate 从拉丁语的「工具」义长出来。

items.example: Fumigation names the process.
items.exampleCN: fumigation 命名这一过程。

items.example: Perfume joins per- through with fumare to smoke.
items.exampleCN: perfume 由 per-（穿过）与 fumare（冒烟）组合而成。

definition_zh: 真菌；菌类；霉层；真菌感染
definition_en: a living thing such as a mushroom, mold, or yeast that feeds on organic matter and is neither plant nor animal
core_image: 潮湿角落里一层毛茸茸的白色霉斑，正缓慢铺开
scene: 雨后的木箱没有晾干，箱盖内侧浮出一片灰白色的霉层。After the rain, a patch of fungus spread across the damp lid of the wooden box.
sceneCN: 这里 fungus 是「真菌」（第 1 个义项：霉菌、蘑菇、酵母这类生物）；句意：雨后木箱没有晾干，箱盖内侧浮出一片真菌。

pos.zh: 真菌；菌类；霉菌

derivatives.zh: 真菌的；由 fungus 加形容词后缀 -al 构成
杀真菌剂；由 fungus 与表示「杀」的 -cide 复合
真菌性的；来自拉丁语 fungosus，偏向菌体本身的性质
菌样的；由 fungus 加 -oid（像……的）构成

senses.title: A member of the kingdom Fungi
senses.definition: a living organism that feeds on organic matter and is neither plant nor animal
senses.definitionCN: 以有机物为食、既不属于植物也不属于动物的生物
senses.example: Fungi break down dead leaves in the forest soil.
senses.exampleCN: 真菌在森林土壤里分解枯叶。
senses.why: Latin fungus first named a mushroom, and biology later widened the word to the whole kingdom.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 fungus 本指蘑菇，后来的生物学把这个词扩大到整个真菌界，所以核心意象里那层霉其实是整整一类生物。

senses.title: A visible growth of mold
senses.definition: a soft or powdery growth of mold on damp material
senses.definitionCN: 潮湿物体表面长出的柔软或粉状的霉
senses.example: A white fungus had grown over the bread.
senses.exampleCN: 面包上已经长出一层白色的霉。
senses.why: The mushroom picture shrinks to the fuzzy patch seen on damp wood, bread, and cellar walls.
senses.whyCN: 蘑菇的画面缩小成受潮木头、面包和地下室墙上那层毛茸茸的斑块，于是 fungus 也直接指看得见的霉层。

senses.title: A fungal infection
senses.definition: an infection of the skin or nails caused by a fungus
senses.definitionCN: 由真菌引起的皮肤或指甲感染
senses.example: He picked up a fungus at the gym shower.
senses.exampleCN: 他在健身房的淋浴间染上了真菌。
senses.why: Because fungi thrive in warm damp places, the same word came to name the infection itself.
senses.whyCN: 真菌爱在温暖潮湿处繁殖，人们便用同一个词直接指这种感染，于是义项从「菌」转到「由菌引起的病」。

senses.title: A plant disease caused by fungi
senses.definition: a disease of crops or plants caused by fungal growth
senses.definitionCN: 由真菌生长引起的作物或植物病害
senses.example: The potato crop was hit by a fungus last summer.
senses.exampleCN: 去年夏天马铃薯作物遭了真菌病害。
senses.why: Farmers met the same organism as a blight on leaves and tubers, so the word took that sense too.
senses.whyCN: 农民在叶片和块茎上遇到的还是同一种生物，只是它此时是一场病害，于是 fungus 又指作物身上的真菌病害。

senses.title: Something that spreads quietly
senses.definition: a harmful thing that spreads unnoticed, like mold in a damp room
senses.definitionCN: 像潮湿房间里的霉一样不知不觉扩散的有害事物
senses.example: Corruption is a fungus that grows in closed systems.
senses.exampleCN: 腐败是在封闭体系里生长的一种霉菌。
senses.why: The mold image is borrowed for hidden problems that spread silently in the dark.
senses.whyCN: 霉层总在暗处慢慢铺开，这个画面被借去形容无声扩散的隐患，于是有了比喻义。

intro.en: Fungus comes straight from Latin fungus, a mushroom, and the deeper link to Greek spongos, a sponge, is uncertain.
intro.cn: fungus 直接来自拉丁语 fungus（蘑菇），再往前的线索是否通到希腊语 spongos（海绵），学界并无定论。

items.en: Greek spongos names a sponge, and some scholars treat it as the older shape behind Latin fungus.
items.cn: 希腊语 spongos 指海绵，部分学者认为它是拉丁语 fungus 更早的来源形态。

items.en: Classical Latin fungus names a mushroom and also a growth on trees.
items.cn: 古典拉丁语的 fungus 既指蘑菇，也指树上长出的菌状物。

items.en: Writers such as Pliny use fungus for edible and poisonous mushrooms alike.
items.cn: 普林尼等作家用 fungus 兼指可食与有毒的蘑菇。

items.en: Fungus picks up a second sense in Latin, a dull or slow-witted fellow.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语里 fungus 多出一个义项，指迟钝呆板的人。

items.en: English borrows fungus as a learned word for mushrooms and molds.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪把 fungus 借进来，作为指蘑菇与霉菌的学术用词。

items.en: Modern biology makes Fungi a kingdom of its own, apart from plants.
items.cn: 现代生物学把真菌单列为独立的一界，与植物分开。

note.en: Fungus sits inside a tight English family of fungal, fungous, and fungicide, and beside the everyday mold words.
note.cn: fungus 处在一个紧密的英语词族里，周围是 fungal、fungous、fungicide，旁边则是日常说霉的几个词。

entries.definition: relating to fungi
entries.definitionCN: 真菌的；由 fungus 加 -al 构成，词源相同

entries.definition: of the nature of a fungus
entries.definitionCN: 真菌性的；来自拉丁语 fungosus，与 fungus 同源

entries.definition: a substance that kills fungi
entries.definitionCN: 杀真菌剂；由 fungus 与 -cide 复合而成

entries.definition: a soft green or white growth on stale food
entries.definitionCN: 霉；多指食物上的霉层，日常可与 fungus 换用

entries.definition: the fleshy fruiting body of a fungus
entries.definitionCN: 蘑菇；真菌的伞状子实体
