entries.definition: a single-celled fungus used in baking and brewing
entries.definitionCN: 酵母；用于发面和酿造的单细胞真菌

normalIntro.en: Fungus is held by the picture of a fuzzy patch spreading over something damp, and by its family of fungal words.
normalIntro.cn: 记住 fungus，可以抓住「潮湿处铺开的绒毛」这幅画面，再顺着 fungal 这一族词一起记。

normal.en: Fungus and fungi are one word in two numbers, so scientific prose keeps the Latin plural.
normal.cn: fungus 与 fungi 是同一个词的单复数，学术文章沿用拉丁式复数。

normal.en: A fungus infection is the everyday phrase for stubborn skin and nail problems.
normal.cn: fungus infection 是日常说法，指反复难好的皮肤与指甲问题。

normal.en: Fungicide joins fungus with -cide, a suffix that means killing.
normal.cn: fungicide 把 fungus 与表示「杀」的后缀 -cide 组合在一起。

normal.en: Fungal is the adjective, so we say a fungal spore rather than a fungus spore.
normal.cn: fungal 是形容词，所以常说 fungal spore 而不太说 fungus spore。

normal.en: Fungi are neither plants nor animals, which is why biology gives them a kingdom of their own.
normal.cn: 真菌既不是植物也不是动物，所以生物学给它单独一界。

abstract.en: See a mushroom cap and a bread mold as two faces of one family.
abstract.cn: 想象蘑菇的伞盖与面包上的霉斑，其实是同一族的两副面孔。

abstract.en: Watch a white fuzz creep over an orange left too long in the fruit bowl.
abstract.cn: 想象果盘里放太久的橙子上慢慢爬满一层白绒毛。

abstract.en: Picture a red itching ring between two toes after a shower.
abstract.cn: 想象淋浴后脚趾间出现一圈发红发痒的癣。

examples.en: The walls were covered with fungus after the flood.
examples.cn: 洪水过后，墙上长满了真菌。

examples.en: Athletes often pick up a fungus between their toes.
examples.cn: 运动员常在脚趾间染上真菌。

examples.en: Fungi break down dead leaves in the forest soil.
examples.cn: 真菌在森林土壤里分解枯叶。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「芳格斯」——听起来像「房里发霉的角落」，想象潮气里冒出的一小片白斑；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 fungus（蘑菇）→ 英语 fungus；一般认为更早或可追到希腊语 spongos（海绵），但这条线索存疑，核心义始终是「菌」。

sensesIntro.en: Fungus begins as a mushroom word, widens to the whole biological kingdom, then names the visible mold, the infection, the crop disease, and finally a hidden thing that spreads.
sensesIntro.cn: fungus 先是一个「蘑菇」词，随后扩大到整个生物类群，再指看得见的霉层、感染、作物病害，最后引申为无声扩散的隐患。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fuzzy white patch spreading over a damp corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：潮湿角落里不断铺开的白色绒毛。

branches.en: The biological kingdom is the widest sense of the word.
branches.cn: 生物类群是这个词范围最广的义项。

branches.en: The visible mold patch is the sense we can see.
branches.cn: 看得见的霉层是最具画面感的义项。

branches.en: The infection sense moves from the organism to the illness.
branches.cn: 感染义把重心从生物本身移到了病症。

branches.en: The crop disease sense applies the same organism to farming.
branches.cn: 作物病害义把同一种生物放到农业场景里。

branches.en: A quiet spreading problem borrows the growth habit of fungi.
branches.cn: 无声蔓延的隐患，借用的正是真菌的生长方式。

intro.en: Fungus is a Latin noun that English kept almost unchanged, and it grew a family of fungal, fungous, fungicide, and fungoid.
intro.cn: fungus 是一个几乎原样进入英语的拉丁语名词，并长出了 fungal、fungous、fungicide、fungoid 这一族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin fungus means a mushroom, and fungosus means full of mushrooms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fungus 意为蘑菇，fungosus 意为长满蘑菇的。

items.example: Latin fungus is the direct source of the English word.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 fungus 是英语这个词的直接来源。

items.example: Fungosus supplies the older adjective behind fungous.
items.exampleCN: fungosus 提供了 fungous 背后的早期形容词。

items.example: Fungi is the Latin plural kept in English science.
items.exampleCN: fungi 是英语科学写作保留的拉丁式复数。

items.example: The suffix -al turns fungus into fungal.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 把 fungus 变成 fungal。

items.example: Fungal describes spores, growth, and infections.
items.exampleCN: fungal 描述孢子、生长与感染。

items.example: The suffix -cide appears in fungicide.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -cide 出现在 fungicide 里。

items.example: Fungicide is sprayed on crops to stop mold.
items.exampleCN: fungicide 被喷在作物上以阻止霉病。

items.example: The suffix -oid forms fungoid.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -oid 构成了 fungoid。

items.example: Fungoid describes a fungus-like growth.
items.exampleCN: fungoid 形容像真菌一样的增生物。

latinEntries.example: Fungosus stands behind the English fungous.
latinEntries.exampleCN: fungosus 是英语 fungous 的前身。

definition_zh: 消沉；霉味；惊恐；放克乐
definition_en: a low mood, a strong stale smell, a state of panic, or a style of dance music with a heavy bass groove
core_image: 一间久未开窗的屋子，闷着一股散不掉的潮味
scene: 连着几周他提不起劲，朋友说他陷进了低谷。After losing the match, he sat in a funk for days and spoke to no one.
sceneCN: 这里 funk 是「低落消沉」（第 1 个义项：一阵抑郁的状态）；句意：输掉比赛后，他消沉了好几天，谁都不理。

pos.zh: 消沉；霉味；惊恐；放克乐

derivatives.zh: 有霉味的；放克的；由 funk 加 -y 构成，词义从气味扩到音乐风格
霉味；放克味；由 funky 加 -ness 构成，指那种土气而带劲的质感

senses.title: A low mood that will not lift
senses.definition: a period of sadness or depression in which someone withdraws
senses.definitionCN: 一段悲伤或抑郁、不愿与人来往的时期
senses.example: He has been in a funk since the project failed.
senses.exampleCN: 项目失败后，他一直消沉着。
senses.why: The smell sense darkened into a mood sense: a funk is an atmosphere that hangs over a person.
senses.whyCN: 气味义转向情绪义：funk 像一股散不掉的空气，罩在一个人头上，于是指挥之不去的低落。

senses.title: A strong unpleasant smell
senses.definition: a strong, stale, and unpleasant smell
senses.definitionCN: 浓烈、陈旧而难闻的气味
senses.example: A heavy funk of old tobacco filled the room.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里弥漫着一股旧烟草的浓重气味。
senses.why: The oldest recorded sense is a smell, probably from a word for smoking or smoke.
senses.whyCN: 有记录的最早义项就是气味，可能来自表示「冒烟」的词，所以核心画面是闷住不散的空气。

senses.title: A state of panic or fear
senses.definition: a state of fear or panic, especially in the fixed phrase blue funk
senses.definitionCN: 恐惧或惊慌的状态，常见于 blue funk 这一说法
senses.example: The recruits were in a blue funk before the inspection.
senses.exampleCN: 检查之前，新兵们慌作一团。
senses.why: British slang turned the low mood into panic, because fear also empties a person out.
senses.whyCN: 英国俚语把低落推成惊恐，因为恐惧同样会让人像被抽空一样，于是「闷住」的画面升级为「吓住」。

senses.title: A style of dance music
senses.definition: a style of popular music with a strong bass groove and syncopated rhythm
senses.definitionCN: 一种低音强烈、节奏切分的流行音乐风格
senses.example: The horn section brought a raw funk to the closing number.
senses.exampleCN: 管乐组给压轴曲目带来了一股粗粝的放克味。
senses.why: Jazz slang called earthy music funky, and funk became the name of the style itself.
senses.whyCN: 爵士乐俚语把土气、带劲的音乐叫 funky，后来 funk 直接成了这种音乐风格的名字，源头仍是那股「土味」。

senses.title: An earthy, hard-driving quality
senses.definition: the earthy, raw quality that jazz players admired in a performance
senses.definitionCN: 爵士乐手所欣赏的那种土气而带劲的质感
senses.example: There was funk in the way the drummer laid into the beat.
senses.exampleCN: 鼓手砸进节拍的方式里有股放克的劲。
senses.why: Before funk named a genre, it named the down-home quality players heard in a groove.
senses.whyCN: 在 funk 成为乐种名之前，它先指乐手在律动里听到的那种乡土而粗粝的质感，所以义项落在「演奏的味道」上。

intro.en: Funk has two strands: a smell word of uncertain origin, and a mood word from British slang, with the music sense growing out of the smell.
intro.cn: funk 有两条线索：一条是来源不确定的气味词，一条是英国俚语里的情绪词，音乐义则从气味义长出来。

items.en: The smell sense may trace back to Latin fumus, smoke, though the link is not certain.
items.cn: 气味义可能上溯到拉丁语 fumus（烟），但这条线索并不确定。

items.en: Old French funkiere, to smoke, is often named as the middle link.
items.cn: 古法语 funkiere（冒烟）常被视为中间的连接环节。

items.en: Funk appears in English writing as a word for a strong stale smell.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语文献里，funk 指浓烈陈旧的气味。

items.en: By the eighteenth century funk also means fear and a low mood.
items.cn: 到十八世纪，funk 又指恐惧与情绪低落。

items.en: Jazz players call earthy, hard-driving music funky.
items.cn: 爵士乐手把土气而带劲的音乐称作 funky。

items.en: Funk becomes the label of a bass-driven dance style.
items.cn: funk 成为以低音驱动的舞蹈音乐风格之名。

note.en: Funk keeps a small family of funky and funkiness, and stands near gloom, panic, and earthy music words.
note.cn: funk 的词族很小，只有 funky 与 funkiness，意思上则靠近表示忧郁、惊慌和土气音乐的几个词。

entries.definition: having a strong smell, or in a raw dance-music style
entries.definitionCN: 有浓烈气味的；放克风格的；由 funk 加 -y 构成

entries.definition: the quality of being funky
entries.definitionCN: 霉味；放克味；由 funky 加 -ness 构成

entries.definition: to fill a space with smoke or vapor in order to disinfect it
entries.definitionCN: 烟熏消毒；与 funk 的气味义可能同出拉丁语 fumus（烟），但英语里各自独立发展

entries.definition: a feeling of deep sadness and hopelessness
a state of low spirits and inactivity
entries.definitionCN: 低气压般的消沉；无精打采

entries.definition: sudden uncontrollable fear

normalIntro.en: Funk is one word with three temperatures: a smell, a mood, and a groove, all sharing the idea of something heavy that will not clear.
normalIntro.cn: funk 一个词有三种温度：气味、情绪与律动，共通点是「沉甸甸、散不掉」。

normal.en: In a funk is the fixed phrase for a low mood that will not lift.
normal.cn: in a funk 是固定说法，指久久不退的低落。

normal.en: Blue funk is the older British phrase for a deep gloom or a panic.
normal.cn: blue funk 是较早的英国说法，指深度沮丧或惊慌。

normal.en: Because funk also names a smell, a room can have the funk of stale smoke.
normal.cn: funk 也指气味，所以说一间屋子有陈旧烟味的 funk。

normal.en: Funky is the adjective from funk, first for smell and later for music.
normal.cn: funky 是 funk 的形容词，先指气味，后来指音乐。

normal.en: Jazz players gave funk its musical sense, meaning an earthy, hard-driving groove.
normal.cn: 爵士乐手给了 funk 音乐义，指土气而带劲的律动。

abstract.en: Picture a grey room where the curtains have stayed shut for weeks.
abstract.cn: 想象一间灰暗的屋子，窗帘几周都没拉开。

abstract.en: Think of a gym bag left in a locker over the holidays.
abstract.cn: 想象假期里被忘在储物柜里的运动包。

abstract.en: See a soldier freeze when the whistle suddenly blows.
abstract.cn: 想象哨声突然响起时，一名士兵僵在原地。

examples.en: He has been in a funk since the project failed.
examples.cn: 项目失败后，他一直消沉着。

examples.en: A heavy funk of old tobacco filled the room.
examples.cn: 房间里弥漫着一股旧烟草的浓重气味。

examples.en: The horn section brought a raw funk to the closing number.
examples.cn: 管乐组给压轴曲目带来了一股粗粝的放克味。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「放克」——这正是中文给这种音乐类型的译名；想象一间闷了很久的屋子，气味与情绪一起压下来；这只是谐音与联想，与词源无关。

root: 来源不确定：一说经古法语 funkiere（冒烟）上溯到拉丁语 fumus（烟），先指难闻气味；「忧郁、惊恐」由这股闷住的气味引申，「放克乐」则由「土气带劲」的听感得名。

sensesIntro.en: Funk starts as a smell that will not clear, becomes a mood that will not lift, hardens into panic, and then names an earthy groove and the music built on it.
sensesIntro.cn: funk 从一股散不掉的气味出发，变成退不去的低落，再硬成惊慌，最后指土气带劲的律动以及建立在这律动上的音乐。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shut room full of air that has gone stale.
core.cn: 核心意象：一间关着窗、空气已经闷旧的屋子。

branches.en: A mood that hangs around is the most common sense today.
branches.cn: 久久不散的坏情绪是今天最常用的义项。

branches.en: The smell sense is the oldest recorded one.
branches.cn: 气味义是有记录以来最早的义项。

branches.en: Panic is the mood sense pushed to its extreme.
branches.cn: 惊慌是情绪义被推到极端的产物。

branches.en: The music sense names a whole style, not just a quality.
branches.cn: 音乐义指的是一个完整的风格，而不只是一种质感。

branches.en: The earthy smell and the earthy groove share one word.
branches.cn: 土气的气味与土气的律动共用同一个词。

intro.en: Funk is a short English noun of uncertain origin, and its family is built with -y and -ness rather than with Latin pieces.
intro.cn: funk 是一个来源不确定的简短英语名词，它的词族靠 -y 与 -ness 构成，而不是靠拉丁词素。

latinIntro.en: No Latin word stands directly behind funk; only the smoke word fumus is sometimes suggested as a distant link.
latinIntro.cn: funk 背后没有确凿的拉丁语词，只有表示「烟」的 fumus 有时被提出来作为遥远的线索。

items.example: Fumus is offered as a possible distant source of the smell sense.
items.exampleCN: fumus 被视为气味义可能的遥远来源。

items.example: Fumigare stands behind the English fumigate.
items.exampleCN: fumigare 是英语 fumigate 的前身。

items.example: Old French funkiere is often named as the middle link.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 funkiere 常被视为中间环节。

items.example: Funk first names a smell in English.
items.exampleCN: funk 在英语里最早指气味。

items.example: The suffix -y turns funk into funky.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 把 funk 变成 funky。

items.meaning: smelly, or in a raw dance style
items.example: Funky carries both the smell and the music sense.
items.exampleCN: funky 同时带着气味义与音乐义。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms funkiness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 funkiness。

items.example: Funkiness names the quality, not a single object.
items.exampleCN: funkiness 指这种性质，而不是某个具体东西。

items.example: Funk later names a whole music style.
items.exampleCN: funk 后来指一整个音乐风格。

items.example: Fumigate keeps the old smoke image alive.
items.exampleCN: fumigate 让古老的「烟」意象保留下来。

latinEntries.example: Fumus is a suggested but uncertain link.
latinEntries.exampleCN: fumus 是有人提出但不确定的线索。

latinEntries.example: Fumigare gives English the verb fumigate.
latinEntries.exampleCN: fumigare 给英语提供了动词 fumigate。

definition_zh: 漏斗；烟囱；漏斗状物；汇集；输送
definition_en: a cone-shaped tube used for pouring, a tall chimney on a ship or engine, or to send something through a narrow channel
core_image: 一只锥形漏斗插在瓶口，液体顺着细颈汇成一股
scene: 实验室里，她把浑浊的液体沿着锥形器具倒进细口瓶。In the lab, she poured the cloudy liquid through a funnel into the narrow bottle.
sceneCN: 这里 funnel 是「漏斗」（第 1 个义项：倒液体用的锥形工具）；句意：实验室里，她让浑浊的液体经漏斗流入细口瓶。

pos.zh: 漏斗；烟囱；漏斗状物
汇集；输送；使经窄口通过

derivatives.zh: 漏斗形的；植物学术语，由 funnel 与拉丁语 forma（形状）复合
漏斗状的；由 funnel 与过去分词 shaped 复合
漏斗状结构；解剖学术语，直接借自拉丁语，与 funnel 同源

senses.title: A cone-shaped pouring tool
senses.definition: a tube that is wide at the top and narrow at the bottom, used for pouring liquids
senses.definitionCN: 上宽下窄、用来倾倒液体的器具
senses.example: She poured the batter through a funnel into the cake tin.
senses.exampleCN: 她用漏斗把面糊倒进蛋糕模。
senses.why: Latin infundibulum named a device for pouring in, and the shape has hardly changed since.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 infundibulum 指「往里倒」的器具，形状几百年几乎没变，所以核心画面就是那只锥形漏斗。

senses.title: A chimney on a ship or engine
senses.definition: the tall pipe that carries smoke or exhaust away from a ship, train, or engine
senses.definitionCN: 把烟或废气排出的高烟囱，见于轮船、机车或发动机
senses.example: Smoke rose from the ship funnel into the grey sky.
senses.exampleCN: 烟从轮船烟囱升入灰色的天空。
senses.why: Steam ships wore the same wide-top narrow-base shape, so the tool word was borrowed for the chimney.
senses.whyCN: 蒸汽船的烟囱也是上宽下窄的漏斗形，于是这件工具的名字被借去指烟囱。

senses.title: A funnel-shaped thing or cloud
senses.definition: something shaped like a funnel, such as a tornado cloud reaching the ground
senses.definitionCN: 形状像漏斗的东西，如触地的龙卷云柱
senses.example: A dark funnel touched the field and lifted the dust.
senses.exampleCN: 一道黑色的漏斗云触到田野，把尘土卷了起来。
senses.why: Any narrowing shape can be called a funnel, and weather reports made the funnel cloud familiar.
senses.whyCN: 凡是上宽下窄的形状都能叫 funnel，气象报道让「漏斗云」这个说法变得常见，义项因此从工具转到形状。

senses.title: To gather into one place
senses.definition: to direct money, effort, or resources into a single place or purpose
senses.definitionCN: 把钱、力量或资源引向同一个地方或用途
senses.example: The charity funnelled most of its income into rural clinics.
senses.exampleCN: 这家慈善机构把大部分收入投向了乡村诊所。
senses.why: The verb keeps the pouring image: many streams are narrowed into one flow.
senses.whyCN: 动词义保留「倾倒」的画面：许多股水流被收进一条细流，所以 funnel 表示把分散的东西集中起来。

senses.title: To send along a narrow route
senses.definition: to move people or information through a narrow passage or a fixed channel
senses.definitionCN: 让人员或信息经狭窄通道或固定渠道通过
senses.example: Stewards funnelled the crowd through the side gate.
senses.exampleCN: 引导员把人流引到侧门通过。
senses.why: The narrow neck of the funnel controls the flow, so the verb also means guiding through a channel.
senses.whyCN: 漏斗的细颈控制流速，动词义便延伸为「经渠道引导」，用于人流与信息。

intro.en: Funnel reaches English from Latin infundibulum, a pouring-in device, through Old French and Middle English shortening.
intro.cn: funnel 从拉丁语 infundibulum（往里倒的器具）出发，经古法语与中古英语的缩短形式进入英语。

items.en: Fundere means to pour out, and it stands behind the whole family.
items.cn: fundere 意为倾倒，是整个词族的根。

items.en: Infundibulum names a funnel, literally a thing for pouring in.
items.cn: infundibulum 指漏斗，字面意思是「往里倒的器具」。

items.en: Old French founil shortens the Latin shape for everyday use.
items.cn: 古法语 founil 把拉丁语的长词缩短，方便日常使用。

items.en: Middle English fonel names the kitchen and cellar funnel.
items.cn: 中古英语 fonel 指厨房与地窖用的漏斗。

items.en: Modern English extends funnel to ship chimneys, tornado clouds, and crowded passages.
items.cn: 现代英语把 funnel 扩用到船上的烟囱、龙卷云柱与拥挤的通道。

note.en: Funnel is a Latin pouring word with a small family, and it sits near the everyday words for chimneys and cones.
note.cn: funnel 是一个来自拉丁语「倾倒」的词，词族不大，意思上靠近表示烟囱与锥形的日常词。

entries.definition: a funnel-shaped anatomical structure
entries.definitionCN: 漏斗状的解剖结构；直接来自拉丁语，与 funnel 同源

entries.definition: shaped like a funnel
entries.definitionCN: 漏斗形的；由 funnel 与拉丁语 forma 复合

entries.definition: the bottom of a hollow organ
entries.definitionCN: 中空器官的底部；只是拼写与 funnel 相近，词源不同

entries.definition: a pipe that carries smoke up and out of a building
entries.definitionCN: 烟囱；把烟引出建筑的管道

entries.definition: a shape with a round base and a point at the top
entries.definitionCN: 圆锥；底部为圆、顶端收成尖的形状

entries.definition: a wide container that feeds material into a machine
entries.definitionCN: 料斗；把物料送入机器的宽口容器

normalIntro.en: Funnel is one shape doing many jobs: pouring in a lab, smoking on a ship, spinning in a storm, and squeezing a crowd through a gate.
normalIntro.cn: funnel 是同一个形状在干许多活：实验室里倒液体、轮船上排烟、风暴里旋转、把人群收进一道门。

normal.en: A funnel cloud is the tornado shape that reaches down from the sky.
normal.cn: funnel cloud 就是从天上垂下来的龙卷漏斗。

normal.en: A separating funnel lets a chemist draw off one liquid layer at a time.
normal.cn: separating funnel 让化学家一层一层分出液体。

normal.en: To funnel into is to send money or people toward one point.
normal.cn: funnel into 就是把钱或人引向同一个点。

normal.en: A ship funnel is the tall stack that carries exhaust away.
normal.cn: ship funnel 就是船上那根把废气排走的高烟囱。

normal.en: The whole family goes back to Latin fundere, to pour.
normal.cn: 整个词族都可以追到拉丁语 fundere（倾倒）。

abstract.en: See liquid spinning into a thin thread as it drops through a cone.
abstract.cn: 想象液体穿过锥形口时收成一条细线。

abstract.en: Picture a steamer rolling past with one fat red stack.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘蒸汽船驶过，立着一根粗大的红烟囱。

abstract.en: Watch a dark rope of cloud twist down toward a field.
abstract.cn: 想象一条黑色的云绳扭动着垂向田野。

examples.en: She poured the batter through a funnel into the cake tin.
examples.cn: 她用漏斗把面糊倒进蛋糕模。

examples.en: Smoke rose from the ship funnel into the grey sky.
examples.cn: 烟从轮船烟囱升入灰色的天空。

examples.en: Stewards funnelled the crowd through the side gate.
examples.cn: 引导员把人流引到侧门通过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「方内」——听起来像「方口收进内里」，想象一个大方盆慢慢收成一个细颈小口；这只是谐音联想，不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 fundere（倾倒）→ infundibulum（漏斗）→ 古法语 founil → 中古英语 fonel → 英语 funnel，核心义「把东西收进一个窄口」。

sensesIntro.en: Funnel begins as the pouring tool, passes to chimneys that share its shape, then to any funnel shape in weather, and finally to the verbs of gathering and guiding.
sensesIntro.cn: funnel 先是倾倒用的工具，再指同样形状的烟囱，接着指天气里的漏斗状物，最后发展为「汇集」与「引导」两个动词义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wide mouth narrowing into a thin neck.
core.cn: 核心意象：宽口收成一个细颈。

branches.en: The pouring tool is the literal sense of the word.
branches.cn: 倾倒工具是这个字面义项，也是整条语义链的起点。

branches.en: The ship chimney is a shape match, not a new object.
branches.cn: 船上的烟囱是形状上的对应，而不是新造的物件。

branches.en: Weather reporting turns the shape into a noun of its own.
branches.cn: 气象报道把这个形状本身变成了一个名词。

branches.en: The first verb sense narrows many flows into one.
branches.cn: 第一个动词义把许多股流收成一股。

branches.en: The narrow neck explains both the tool and the guided crowd.
branches.cn: 细颈既解释了工具的作用，也解释了被人为引导的人流。

intro.en: Funnel is the English shortening of a Latin pouring word, and its family is built from fundere and infundibulum.
intro.cn: funnel 是拉丁语「倾倒」词在英语里的缩短形，词族由 fundere 与 infundibulum 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin fundere means to pour, and infundibulum means a funnel.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fundere 意为倾倒，infundibulum 意为漏斗。

items.example: Fundere supplies the pouring image.
items.exampleCN: fundere 提供了「倾倒」的意象。

items.example: The suffix -bulum marks a device, as in infundibulum.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -bulum 标记器具，如 infundibulum。

items.example: Infundibulum is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: infundibulum 是直接的拉丁语来源。

items.example: Old French founil shortens the Latin word.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 founil 把拉丁语词缩短。

items.example: Middle English fonel is the kitchen form.
items.exampleCN: 中古英语 fonel 是厨房里的说法。

items.example: Funnel keeps the tool sense.
items.exampleCN: funnel 保留了工具义。

items.example: Funnel as a verb moves money and crowds.
items.exampleCN: 作动词的 funnel 可以搬动钱与人流。

items.example: Funnel-shaped describes roofs and flowers.
items.exampleCN: funnel-shaped 形容屋顶与花朵。

items.example: Funnelform is the botanical term.
items.exampleCN: funnelform 是植物学的说法。

items.meaning: a tornado cloud shaped like a funnel
items.example: Funnel cloud joins the shape to the weather.
items.exampleCN: funnel cloud 把形状与天气连在一起。

latinEntries.example: Fundere is the root of the whole family.

latinEntries.exampleCN: infundibulum 进入了英语的解剖学词汇。

latinEntries.example: Fundibulum is the shorter variant of the same noun.
latinEntries.exampleCN: fundibulum 是同一个名词的较短变体。

definition_zh: 滑稽演员；喜剧演员；爱逗笑的人
definition_en: a professional comedian, or a man who likes to make other people laugh
core_image: 聚光灯下一个人挤眉弄眼，台下笑成一片
scene: 公司的聚会上，主持人一开口就把全场逗笑。The funnyman at the office party had everyone laughing within a minute.
sceneCN: 这里 funnyman 是「滑稽演员」（第 1 个义项：以逗笑为职业的人）；句意：办公室聚会上的那位滑稽演员一分钟内就让所有人笑了。

pos.zh: 滑稽演员；喜剧演员；爱逗笑的人

derivatives.zh: 好笑的；奇怪的；funnyman 的构词基础，由 fun 加 -y 构成
滑稽地；奇怪地；由 funny 加 -ly 构成
滑稽；好笑；由 funny 加 -ness 构成
女滑稽演员；把 funnyman 的 man 换成 woman 的对等形式

senses.title: A professional comedian
senses.definition: a man whose job is to make an audience laugh
senses.definitionCN: 以逗观众发笑为职业的男子
senses.example: The funnyman kept the audience laughing for an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 那位滑稽演员让观众笑了一个小时。
senses.why: Funny means laughable and man means person, so the compound simply names the man who produces laughter for a living.
senses.whyCN: funny 意为好笑的，man 意为人，复合起来就是「以制造笑声为业的人」，核心画面自然是聚光灯下的逗笑者。

senses.title: The joking man in a group
senses.definition: a man who habitually jokes and entertains the people around him
senses.definitionCN: 习惯开玩笑、逗身边人开心的男子
senses.example: As the family funnyman, he could not let a silence last.
senses.exampleCN: 作为家里的开心果，他见不得冷场。
senses.why: The same compound slides from the stage to ordinary life, where anyone can play the laughing role.
senses.whyCN: 同一个复合词从舞台滑到日常生活，任何愿意扮演逗笑角色的人都能被这样称呼，义项于是从职业转为性格角色。

senses.title: A comic role or character
senses.definition: the humorous character in a play, film, or show
senses.definitionCN: 戏剧、电影或节目里的搞笑角色
senses.example: He played the funnyman while the hero carried the plot.
senses.exampleCN: 他演滑稽角色，主角负责推进剧情。
senses.why: Show business names the role as well as the person, so a script can list a funnyman.
senses.whyCN: 演艺行业既称呼人，也称呼角色，所以剧本里也能把一个角色标成 funnyman，义项从演员转到角色。

senses.title: A humorous writer or broadcaster
senses.titleCN: 幽默作家；搞笑节目主持
senses.definition: a man who writes or presents humorous material for newspapers, radio, or television
senses.definitionCN: 为报纸、广播或电视撰写或主持幽默内容的男子
senses.example: The paper hired a funnyman to write a weekly column.
senses.exampleCN: 这家报纸请了一位幽默作者写每周专栏。
senses.why: Journalism widened the word to anyone who supplies jokes in print or on air, not only on stage.
senses.whyCN: 新闻业把这个词扩用到纸面与电波里提供笑料的人，不再限于舞台，于是义项落在「幽默作者」上。

intro.en: Funnyman is a plain English compound of funny and man, both native Germanic words, with no Latin ingredient.
intro.cn: funnyman 是 funny 与 man 组成的普通英语复合词，两个部分都是英语本族词，没有拉丁语成分。

items.en: Middle English fonne means a foolish person, and dictionaries treat it as the likely source of fun.
items.cn: 中古英语 fonne 指愚笨的人，词典一般把它视为 fun 的可能来源。

items.en: Fun first names a trick or a joke rather than simple amusement.
items.cn: 十七世纪时，fun 先指把戏或玩笑，而不是单纯的娱乐。

items.en: Funny appears as an adjective for something odd, and soon for something amusing.
items.cn: 十八世纪 funny 作形容词，先指古怪，很快也指好笑。

items.en: Funnyman is formed on the model of funny plus man for a comic performer.
items.cn: 十九世纪按 funny 加 man 的模式造出 funnyman，指滑稽演员。

items.en: American show business and newspapers spread funnyman to columnists and talk-show hosts.
items.cn: 美国演艺圈与报纸把 funnyman 扩用到专栏作者与脱口秀主持。

note.en: Funnyman is built from the native funny family, and its nearest neighbours are the words for comedians and clowns.
note.cn: funnyman 由本族词 funny 一族构成，意思上最贴近表示喜剧演员与小丑的几个词。

entries.definition: causing laughter, or strange
entries.definitionCN: 好笑的；奇怪的；funnyman 的构词基础

entries.definition: in a funny or odd way
entries.definitionCN: 滑稽地；古怪地；由 funny 加 -ly 构成

entries.definition: a female comedian
entries.definitionCN: 女滑稽演员；与 funnyman 结构对等

entries.definition: a person who performs comedy
entries.definitionCN: 喜剧演员；funnyman 最直接的近义词

entries.definition: a performer who makes people laugh
entries.definitionCN: 滑稽演员；也可指喜剧的

entries.definition: a performer in make-up who plays the fool
entries.definitionCN: 小丑；化妆扮演傻瓜的表演者

normalIntro.en: Funnyman is simply funny plus man, and the plural swaps man for men, so the word explains itself.
normalIntro.cn: funnyman 就是 funny 加 man，复数把 man 换成 men，这个词几乎能自己解释自己。

normal.en: Funny gives the laughter and man gives the person, so the compound is transparent.
normal.cn: funny 提供笑声，man 提供人，复合词的意思一目了然。

normal.en: The plural is funnymen, changing man to men like other compounds.
normal.cn: 复数是 funnymen，和其他含 man 的复合词一样把 man 改成 men。

normal.en: Funny goes back to fun, which first meant a trick or a joke.
normal.cn: funny 可追到 fun，而 fun 最早指把戏或玩笑。

normal.en: Funnyman belongs mainly to show-business and newspaper prose.
normal.cn: funnyman 主要出现在演艺报道与报纸文字里。

normal.en: Funnywoman is the matching form when the performer is a woman.
normal.cn: 表演者是女性时，对应写法是 funnywoman。

abstract.en: Picture a single spotlight and a man pulling faces at the front of the stage.
abstract.cn: 想象一束聚光灯，一个人站在台口不断做鬼脸。

abstract.en: See a dinner table go quiet until one man tells a story and everyone cracks up.
abstract.cn: 想象饭桌忽然冷场，一个人讲了段故事，全桌笑翻。

abstract.en: Think of a script page with one line marked comic relief.
abstract.cn: 想象剧本某一页标着「滑稽角色」的那一行。

examples.en: The funnyman kept the audience laughing for an hour.
examples.cn: 那位滑稽演员让观众笑了一个小时。

examples.en: As the family funnyman, he could not let a silence last.
examples.cn: 作为家里的开心果，他见不得冷场。

examples.en: Two funnymen traded jokes on the late-night show.
examples.cn: 两位笑星在深夜节目里互相抛笑话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「发尼曼」——「发尼」听着像 funny（好笑的），后面拖着一个 man（人），合起来就是逗笑的人；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 英语复合词：funny（好笑的，源自 fun「玩笑、把戏」）+ man（人）→ funnyman，字面就是「逗笑的人」，复数写作 funnymen。

sensesIntro.en: Funnyman starts on the stage as a working comedian, moves into any group with a resident joker, then names the comic role in a script, and finally the humour writer in print or on air.
sensesIntro.cn: funnyman 从舞台上的职业喜剧演员出发，走进任何一个有开心果的圈子，再指剧本里的滑稽角色，最后指纸面与电波里的幽默作者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one man under a spotlight making a whole room laugh.
core.cn: 核心意象：聚光灯下一个人把整屋子人逗笑。

branches.en: The stage professional is the sense the word was coined for.
branches.cn: 舞台上的职业演员是这个词最初被造出来时的义项。

branches.en: The group joker is the same role played for free.
branches.cn: 圈子里的开心果，是把同一角色免费地演在生活里。

branches.en: The comic role turns the person into a part in a script.
branches.cn: 滑稽角色义把「人」变成剧本里的一个行当。

branches.en: The humour writer performs the same job without a stage.
branches.cn: 幽默作者没有舞台，却做着同一件事。

branches.en: A performer and a written role are two sides of one comic function.
branches.cn: 演员与纸上的角色，是同一个逗笑功能的两个侧面。

intro.en: Funnyman has no Latin inside it: it is built from the native words fun, funny, and man, with the irregular plural funnymen.
intro.cn: funnyman 里面没有拉丁语成分，它由本族词 fun、funny、man 构成，复数是不规则的 funnymen。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source for funnyman, so the Latin entries are left empty on purpose.
latinIntro.cn: funnyman 没有拉丁语来源，因此拉丁同源词一栏有意留空。

items.example: Fun first meant a trick more than simple pleasure.
items.exampleCN: fun 最早更多指把戏，而不是单纯的快乐。

items.example: The suffix -y turns fun into funny.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -y 把 fun 变成 funny。

items.example: Funny describes what makes people laugh.
items.exampleCN: funny 形容让人发笑的东西。

items.example: Funny also means slightly odd.
items.exampleCN: funny 也可以指有点古怪。

items.example: Man supplies the person in the compound.
items.exampleCN: man 为复合词提供了「人」这一部分。

items.example: Funnyman joins the two words into one trade.
items.exampleCN: funnyman 把两个词合成一门行当。

items.meaning: the plural of man in compounds
items.meaningCN: 复合词中 man 的复数形式
items.example: The element -men forms the plural funnymen.
items.exampleCN: 成分 -men 构成复数 funnymen。

items.example: Funnymen keeps the old plural pattern.
items.exampleCN: funnymen 保留了古老的复数模式。

items.example: Funnywoman replaces man with woman.
items.exampleCN: funnywoman 把 man 换成了 woman。

definition_zh: 狂怒的；暴怒的；怒气冲冲的；狂暴的
definition_en: raging with fury, or violently angry in look, speech, or manner
core_image: 一个人双眉倒竖、青筋暴起，像一阵风暴压过来
scene: 被当众羞辱后，他整张脸涨红，声音都在抖。The furibund editor tore the letter into pieces and shouted at the clerk.
sceneCN: 这里 furibund 是「狂怒的」（第 1 个义项：处于暴怒状态）；句意：那位狂怒的编辑把信撕成碎片，朝职员大吼。

pos.zh: 狂怒的；暴怒的；狂暴的

derivatives.zh: 狂怒；愤怒；与 furibund 同出拉丁语 furia
狂怒的；激烈的；由拉丁语 furiosus 进入英语，与 furibund 同源
狂怒；一时的狂热；直接借自拉丁语 furor
激怒；使暴怒；由 in- 加拉丁语 furia 的词根构成

senses.title: Raging with fury
senses.definition: in a state of violent, uncontrolled anger
senses.definitionCN: 处于猛烈、无法自控的愤怒之中
senses.example: The furibund coach paced the touchline and shouted at every mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 狂怒的教练沿着边线来回走，每次失误都大吼。
senses.why: Latin furibundus describes a person seized by furor, so the adjective pictures rage as a force that takes hold of someone.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 furibundus 形容被 furor 抓住的人，所以这个形容词把愤怒画成一股把人攥住的力量，核心画面正是那张暴怒的脸。

senses.title: Angry in speech or look
senses.definition: carrying or showing violent anger in words, tone, or expression
senses.definitionCN: 在言语、语气或神情里透出猛烈怒气的
senses.example: Her furibund reply arrived the same evening.
senses.exampleCN: 她那封火气冲天的回信当晚就到了。
senses.why: The adjective spreads from the raging person to the things that person produces, such as a letter or a speech.
senses.whyCN: 形容词从发怒的人扩散到他产出的东西，如书信与演讲，于是义项落在「带着怒气的言语神情」上。

senses.title: Raging like a storm
senses.definition: violent and uncontrolled, as of a storm or the elements
senses.definitionCN: 像风暴或自然力那样猛烈而失控的
senses.example: Even the furibund storm could not stop the rescue team.
senses.exampleCN: 连那场狂暴的风暴也没能挡住救援队。
senses.why: Writers lend the human rage to weather, so a gale or a sea can be called furibund in literary prose.
senses.whyCN: 作家把人身上的狂怒借给天气，于是狂风与怒海在文学作品里也能叫 furibund，义项从人转到自然力。

senses.title: Frenzied, carried away
senses.definition: frenzied or wildly enthusiastic, as if possessed by a raging force
senses.definitionCN: 近乎发狂或极度狂热，像被一股狂暴的力量附身
senses.example: The crowd gave the singer a furibund welcome.
senses.exampleCN: 人群给了那位歌手近乎癫狂的欢迎。
senses.why: Because furor also means frenzy rather than plain anger, the adjective can describe any carried-away state.
senses.whyCN: 因为 furor 除了愤怒也指狂热，这个形容词便能用来说明任何「失去分寸」的状态，义项从怒气延伸到癫狂的热情。

intro.en: Furibund comes from Latin furibundus, an adjective of raging, built on furere, to rave.
intro.cn: furibund 来自拉丁语 furibundus，一个表示狂怒的形容词，词根是 furere（发狂）。

items.en: Furere means to rage, to rave, or to be out of one mind.
items.cn: furere 意为暴怒、发狂、失去理智。

items.en: The suffix -bundus marks a person full of an action, so furibundus means full of raging.
items.cn: 词尾 -bundus 表示「充满某种动作的人」，所以 furibundus 意为「充满狂怒的」。

items.en: Cicero and the poets use furibundus for raging people and raging seas.
items.cn: 西塞罗与诗人们用 furibundus 形容暴怒的人，也形容狂暴的海。

items.en: Furia, fury, and furor grow from the same root and supply the English family.
items.cn: furia（狂怒女神）与 furor 同出这个词根，为英语提供了同族词。

items.en: English adopts furibund as a literary adjective for violent anger.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入 furibund，作为文学性的「暴怒」形容词。

items.en: The word survives mainly in dictionaries, translations, and deliberately archaic prose.
items.cn: 这个词主要活在词典、译文与有意仿古的文字里。

note.en: Furibund belongs to the Latin fury family and stands beside the everyday angry words, though it is far more literary.
note.cn: furibund 属于拉丁语「狂怒」词族，意思上挨着日常表示生气的几个词，但文体色彩要浓得多。

entries.definition: extremely angry
entries.definitionCN: 狂怒的；与 furibund 同出拉丁语 furia

entries.definition: violent anger
a burst of rage or wild enthusiasm
entries.definitionCN: 狂怒；一时的狂热；直接借自拉丁语

entries.definition: angry, especially in a formal or slightly humorous tone
entries.definitionCN: 恼怒的；偏正式或略带调侃的「生气」

entries.definition: very angry, or violent and uncontrolled
entries.definitionCN: 暴怒的；也指猛烈失控的

entries.definition: extremely angry
entries.definitionCN: 气得脸色发青的；极度愤怒的

normalIntro.en: Furibund is the rarest branch of a familiar family: furere rages, furia is fury, and furibundus is full of that rage.
normalIntro.cn: furibund 是一个熟悉词族里最冷门的一支：furere 是发狂，furia 是狂怒，furibundus 就是充满这股狂怒。

normal.en: The root furere means to rave, and fury, furious, and furor all come from it.
normal.cn: 词根 furere 意为发狂，fury、furious、furor 都从它来。

normal.en: The Latin suffix -bundus means full of an action, so furibund is literally full of raging.
normal.cn: 拉丁词尾 -bundus 表示「充满某种动作」，所以 furibund 字面就是「充满狂怒」。

normal.en: Furibund is a literary adjective, so it turns up in translations and old-style prose.
normal.cn: furibund 是文学性形容词，多见于译文与仿古文字。

normal.en: A furibund rage is a fixed, almost tautological pairing that writers use for emphasis.
normal.cn: furibund rage 几乎是同义叠加，作家用它来加重语气。

normal.en: Compare furious: furious is everyday, furibund is rare and bookish.
normal.cn: 对比 furious：furious 日常通用，furibund 罕见且书面。

abstract.en: See a red face with the veins standing out at the temples.
abstract.cn: 想象一张涨红的脸，太阳穴上的青筋都鼓起来。

abstract.en: Picture a letter torn in half and thrown across a desk.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信被撕成两半，摔在桌面上。

abstract.en: Watch a black squall line push across the sea without a pause.
abstract.cn: 想象一道黑色的飑线不停顿地压过海面。

examples.en: The furibund coach paced the touchline and shouted at every mistake.
examples.cn: 狂怒的教练沿着边线来回走，每次失误都大吼。

examples.en: Her furibund reply arrived the same evening.
examples.cn: 她那封火气冲天的回信当晚就到了。

examples.en: Even the furibund storm could not stop the rescue team.
examples.cn: 连那场狂暴的风暴也没能挡住救援队。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弗瑞邦德」——前一半听着像 furious（狂怒），后一半听着像 bound（被捆住），合起来像「被怒气捆住的人」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 furere（发狂、暴怒）→ 词尾 -bundus（充满……的）→ furibundus（狂怒的）→ 英语 furibund；同族还有 fury、furious、furor、infuriate。

sensesIntro.en: Furibund begins with the raging person, passes to the angry words and looks that person produces, is lent to storms in literary prose, and finally widens to any frenzied state.
sensesIntro.cn: furibund 先写暴怒的人，再写这人的言语神情，文学作品把它借给风暴，最后扩到任何近乎癫狂的状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a face flushed with rage, like a storm about to break.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张因暴怒而涨红的脸，像随时炸开的风暴。

branches.en: The raging person is the original Latin sense.
branches.cn: 暴怒的人是最初的拉丁语义项。

branches.en: Angry words and looks carry the rage outward.
branches.cn: 怒气冲冲的言语神情，把狂怒向外传递。

branches.en: Literary prose lends the human rage to weather.
branches.cn: 文学作品把人的狂怒借给了天气。

branches.en: Frenzy is rage without a target, pushed to pure intensity.
branches.cn: 癫狂是没有具体对象的怒气，被推到纯粹的强度。

branches.en: A furious man and a furious gale share one adjective.
branches.cn: 暴怒的人与狂暴的大风共用一个形容词。

intro.en: Furibund is a Latin adjective imported whole, and its family is built on furere and the suffix -bundus.
intro.cn: furibund 是整个借入的拉丁语形容词，词族建立在 furere 与词尾 -bundus 上。

latinIntro.en: Latin furere means to rage, furibundus means raging, and -bundus means full of an action.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 furere 意为发狂，furibundus 意为狂怒的，-bundus 意为充满某种动作。

items.example: Furere supplies the rage behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: furere 提供了整个词族背后的那股怒气。

items.example: The suffix -bundus shapes furibundus.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -bundus 构成了 furibundus。

items.example: Furibundus is the direct source of furibund.
items.exampleCN: furibundus 是 furibund 的直接来源。

items.example: Furia gives English the noun fury.
items.exampleCN: furia 给英语提供了名词 fury。

items.example: Furor enters English unchanged.
items.exampleCN: furor 原样进入英语。

items.example: Fury is the everyday noun of the family.
items.exampleCN: fury 是这一族里最日常的名词。

items.example: Furious is the common adjective, furibund the rare one.
items.exampleCN: furious 是常见的形容词，furibund 则罕见。

items.example: Infuriate puts the family into verb form.
items.exampleCN: infuriate 把这个词族变成动词。

items.example: Furibund keeps the full Latin shape.
items.exampleCN: furibund 保留了完整的拉丁语词形。

latinEntries.example: Furibundus passes into English as furibund.
latinEntries.exampleCN: furibundus 以 furibund 的形式进入英语。

latinEntries.example: Furia stands behind the English fury.
latinEntries.exampleCN: furia 是英语 fury 的前身。

latinEntries.example: Furor is borrowed whole into English.

definition_zh: 狂怒的；暴怒的；猛烈的；激烈的；飞速的
definition_en: extremely angry, or very violent, intense, or fast in action
core_image: 烧到壶口的水：怒气顶到极限，随时溢出
scene: 餐厅里有人插队，排了很久的客人一下子火了。The customer was furious at the waiter for letting someone jump the queue.
sceneCN: 这里 furious 是「狂怒的」（第 1 个义项：极度生气）；句意：那位顾客因为服务员让别人插队而对他大发雷霆。

pos.zh: 形容词：狂怒的；暴怒的；猛烈的；激烈的；飞速的

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「狂怒地；猛烈地」
与本词同源的拉丁语名词，义为「狂怒；猛烈」
由本词加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「狂怒；猛烈」
由前缀 in- 加同源词根构成，义为「使大怒；激怒」

senses.title: Extremely angry
senses.definition: feeling or showing very great anger that is hard to control
senses.definitionCN: 感到或表现出难以控制的极度愤怒
senses.example: She was furious when the train was cancelled without notice.
senses.exampleCN: 列车毫无通知就取消，她气得要命。
senses.why: Latin furia names raging madness, and the adjective furiosus means full of that rage; furious keeps the picture of anger burning out of control.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 furia 指「狂乱的暴怒」，形容词 furiosus 意为「充满这种怒气」；furious 保留了怒气烧到失控的画面。

senses.title: Violent and unrestrained
senses.definition: of an attack, argument, or force: very violent and impossible to restrain
senses.definitionCN: 指攻击、争论或力量极为猛烈、无法遏制的
senses.example: The defenders faced a furious attack before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 守军在黎明前遭到一场猛烈的进攻。
senses.why: Anger and violence share the same heat: when the rage leaves the body and becomes action, it turns into a furious attack or a furious row.
senses.whyCN: 愤怒与暴力共用同一份热度：怒气离开身体变成行动，就成了猛烈的进攻或激烈的争吵。

senses.title: Very fast and energetic
senses.definition: done at great speed and with great energy
senses.definitionCN: 以极快的速度和极大的精力完成的
senses.example: The team kept up a furious pace in the final minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍在最后几分钟里保持着飞快的节奏。
senses.why: Speed and heat belong together, so a furious pace is activity run at the temperature of anger; the word describes the intensity, not the mood.
senses.whyCN: 速度与热度本就相连，所以 furious pace 是以发怒般的温度进行的活动；这个词描述的是强度，而不是心情。

senses.title: Stormy and wild
senses.definition: of wind, sea, or weather: wild and violent in force
senses.definitionCN: 指风、海面或天气力量狂野而猛烈
senses.example: The furious wind tore the sails to pieces.
senses.exampleCN: 狂暴的风把船帆撕成了碎片。
senses.why: The oldest image of rage is a storm, and English keeps that link: weather with no restraint is called furious just as a person is.
senses.whyCN: 怒气最古老的意象就是风暴，英语保留了这层联系：毫无约束的天气和一个暴怒的人一样，都叫 furious。

intro.en: Furious comes from Latin furiosus, full of rage, from furia, raging madness, and furere, to rave.
intro.cn: furious 来自拉丁语 furiosus（充满怒气），源头是 furia（狂乱）与 furere（发狂）。

items.en: Furere means to rave and to lose control of the mind.
items.cn: furere 意为发狂、失去理智。

items.en: Furia names the raging madness that the gods send.
items.cn: furia 指神明降下的狂乱暴怒。

items.en: Furiosus, full of rage, is the adjective built on furia.
items.cn: furiosus 意为「充满怒气」，是由 furia 构成的形容词。

items.en: Old French furieus carries the adjective north.
items.cn: 古法语 furieus 把这个形容词带到北方。

items.en: Middle English furious keeps the sense of violent anger.
items.cn: 中古英语 furious 保留了暴怒的含义。

items.en: Modern English extends the word to violent attacks, great speed, and stormy weather.
items.cn: 现代英语把词义扩展到猛烈进攻、飞快速度和狂暴天气。

note.en: Furious is the adjective of fury, so the look-alike group holds the rage family, while the near meaning group holds ordinary anger words.
note.cn: furious 是 fury 的形容词，所以形近组收「狂怒」词族，近义组收普通的生气词。

entries.definition: violent, uncontrolled anger
in a violently angry or intense way
to make someone extremely angry
feeling or showing anger
entries.definitionCN: 生气的；愤怒的（程度比 furious 轻）

entries.definition: extremely angry
violent and forceful in action
entries.definitionCN: 凶猛的；猛烈的（偏重力量而非情绪）

normalIntro.en: Furious is the adjective of fury, built on the Latin rage root fur- and finished with the suffix -ious.
normalIntro.cn: furious 是 fury 的形容词，建立在拉丁词根 fur-（狂怒）之上，结尾是后缀 -ious。

normal.en: Furious and fury share one root, so the adjective is simply the noun turned into a description.
normal.cn: furious 与 fury 同根，形容词就是把名词变成描述。

normal.en: You are furious with a person and furious at a thing that annoys you.
normal.cn: 对人用 furious with，对让你恼火的事用 furious at。

normal.en: A furious pace is a speed that feels almost angry.
normal.cn: furious pace 是快得几乎像在发怒的速度。

normal.en: Fast and furious joins speed with force in one fixed phrase.
normal.cn: fast and furious 把速度与力量固定成一个短语。

normal.en: The adverb furiously keeps the same heat and describes how an action is done.
normal.cn: 副词 furiously 保留同样的火气，描述动作怎样进行。

abstract.en: Picture a kettle boiling so hard that water jumps out of the spout.
abstract.cn: 想象一只水壶烧得太猛，水从壶嘴里跳出来。

abstract.en: Picture a door slammed so hard that the windows rattle.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门被摔得极重，窗户都跟着震动。

abstract.en: Picture a runner sprinting the last lap with a red face and clenched fists.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者冲刺最后一圈，脸红着、拳头紧握。

examples.en: He was furious with his brother for losing the keys.
examples.cn: 他因为弟弟弄丢了钥匙而对他大发雷霆。

examples.en: The two sides had a furious argument about the budget.
examples.cn: 双方就预算问题激烈争吵。

examples.en: Work continued at a furious pace until midnight.
examples.cn: 工作以飞快的节奏一直持续到午夜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费油死」——车子费油费到让人暴怒；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 furere（发狂）→ furia（狂乱）→ furiosus（狂怒的）→ 古法语 furieus → 英语 furious，核心义「怒气烧到失控」。

sensesIntro.en: Furious starts with a person in a rage, then moves the same heat into violent action, into great speed, and finally into stormy weather.
sensesIntro.cn: furious 先从一个人暴怒讲起，再把同一份热度移入猛烈行动、飞快速度，最后移入狂暴的天气。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a kettle boiling over, heat with no more room.
core.cn: 核心意象：水壶烧到溢出，热度再无容身之处。

branches.en: A person boiling with anger is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 一个人怒气沸腾，是日常义项。

branches.en: Rage turned into action becomes a violent attack.
branches.cn: 怒气化为行动，就成了猛烈的进攻。

branches.en: Heat read as speed gives the fast pace sense.
branches.cn: 把热度读成速度，就有了飞快的节奏这一义项。

branches.en: The oldest rage image, the storm, survives in weather talk.
branches.cn: 最古老的怒气意象即风暴，仍在天气描述中存活。

branches.en: A furious person and a furious attack are the same anger at two temperatures.
branches.cn: 暴怒的人与猛烈的进攻，是同一份怒气处在两个温度。

intro.en: Furious is built on the Latin rage root fur- with the adjective suffix -ious, and the family spreads through fury, furiously, and infuriate.
intro.cn: furious 由拉丁词根 fur-（狂怒）加形容词后缀 -ious 构成，词族延伸到 fury、furiously 与 infuriate。

latinIntro.en: Latin furere means to rave, furia means raging madness, and furiosus means full of rage.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 furere 意为「发狂」，furia 意为「狂乱」，furiosus 意为「充满怒气」。

items.example: The root fur- carries the heat of rage.
items.exampleCN: 词根 fur- 带着怒气的热度。

items.example: Furia names the madness sent by the gods.
items.exampleCN: furia 指神明降下的狂乱。

items.example: Furere describes a mind out of control.
items.exampleCN: furere 描述失去控制的心智。

items.example: Furiosus is the Latin adjective behind furious.
items.exampleCN: furiosus 是 furious 背后的拉丁语形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ious turns fury into furious.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ious 把 fury 变成 furious。

items.example: Fury is the noun that furious describes.
items.exampleCN: fury 是 furious 所描述的名词。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms furiously.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 furiously。

items.example: Furiously tells how the action is done.
items.exampleCN: furiously 说明动作是怎样进行的。

items.example: The prefix in- plus the rage root gives infuriate.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 加狂怒词根构成 infuriate。

definition_zh: （公众的）狂怒；哗然；狂热；狂乱
definition_en: a state of excited or angry public feeling, or a passionate craze for something
core_image: 人群被同一个念头点着，怒气像火一样传开
scene: 一篇调查报道揭出丑闻，整座城市议论纷纷、怒气冲天。The scandal caused a furor across the country.
sceneCN: 这里 furor 是「公众的哗然与狂怒」（第 1 个义项：众人共同的愤怒与激动）；句意：这桩丑闻在全国引起一片哗然。

pos.zh: 名词：公众的狂怒；哗然；狂热；狂乱

derivatives.zh: 由同源拉丁形容词构成，义为「狂怒的；猛烈的」
由同源拉丁名词构成，义为「狂怒；猛烈」
由前缀 in- 加同源词根构成，义为「使大怒；激怒」

senses.title: Angry public excitement
senses.definition: a state of widespread angry excitement, especially in public life
senses.definitionCN: 广泛蔓延的愤怒与激动，尤指公共生活中的
senses.example: The verdict stirred a furor among civil rights groups.
senses.exampleCN: 这一判决在民权团体中激起一片哗然。
senses.why: The Latin noun furor means madness or rage, and English kept it for rage that spreads through a crowd rather than one chest.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词 furor 意为「狂乱、暴怒」，英语保留它来描述在人群里蔓延、而非只在一人胸中的怒气。

senses.title: A passionate craze
senses.definition: a very enthusiastic and widely shared interest in something, often short-lived
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物非常热烈且广泛共享的兴趣，往往为时短暂
senses.example: The new dance caused a furor among teenagers that summer.
senses.exampleCN: 那支新舞在那个夏天于青少年中掀起一阵狂热。
senses.why: Enthusiasm and anger run at the same heat, so the same word covers a crowd set alight by a fashion instead of an insult.
senses.whyCN: 热情与愤怒的温度相同，所以同一个词也能指被时尚而非侮辱点燃的人群。

senses.title: A fit of frenzy
senses.definition: a state of wild, uncontrolled rage or frenzy in one person
senses.definitionCN: 一个人身上狂野、失控的暴怒或狂乱状态
senses.example: He ran through the streets in a furor, shouting at strangers.
senses.exampleCN: 他狂乱地跑过街道，对着陌生人喊叫。
senses.why: The Latin source names a mind outside itself, so the word still carries the frenzy of one person, not only the anger of a crowd.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源头指「出了窍的心智」，所以这个词仍能指一个人的狂乱，而不只是群体的愤怒。

senses.title: Poetic frenzy
senses.definition: the inspired frenzy that ancient writers believed seized poets and prophets
senses.definitionCN: 古代作家相信会降临在诗人与先知身上的灵感式迷狂
senses.example: Plato described the poet as seized by a divine furor.
senses.exampleCN: 柏拉图把诗人描述为被神灵的迷狂所攫住的人。
senses.why: Ancient thought treated inspiration as possession by a god, and the Latin word for madness was the natural name for that state.
senses.whyCN: 古代思想把灵感看作被神灵附体，而拉丁语中表示「疯狂」的词自然成了这种状态的名称。

intro.en: Furor is Latin furor, madness or rage, from furere, to rave; English borrowed the noun almost unchanged.
intro.cn: furor 就是拉丁语 furor（狂乱、暴怒），源于 furere（发狂）；英语几乎原样借入这个名词。

items.en: Furere means to rave, to be beside oneself.
items.cn: furere 意为发狂、神魂颠倒。

items.en: Furor, the noun of state, means madness or rage.
items.cn: furor 是表示状态的名词，意为狂乱或暴怒。

items.en: Old French furor carries the noun into everyday use.
items.cn: 古法语 furor 把这个名词带入日常使用。

items.en: English borrows furor as a learned word for public rage.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入 furor，作为指公众狂怒的书面词。

items.en: Italian furore enters English in the eighteenth century as a variant.
items.cn: 意大利语 furore 在十八世纪作为异体进入英语。

items.en: Modern English uses furor for scandals, crazes, and public outcry.
items.cn: 现代英语用 furor 指丑闻、风潮与公众的强烈抗议。

note.en: Furor sits in the rage family but always points at a crowd, next to fury for one temper and outcry for the public reaction.
note.cn: furor 属于「狂怒」词族，但总指向人群；旁边有指个人脾气的 fury 与指公众反应的 outcry。

entries.definition: the British spelling of furor
entries.definitionCN: furor 的英式拼写，词源相同

entries.definition: violent anger in one person
extremely angry
a loud public expression of anger or protest
a very popular fashion that lasts a short time
a state of wild excitement or uncontrolled activity
entries.definitionCN: 狂乱；疯狂（偏重失控的行为）

normalIntro.en: Furor is a Latin noun that English took whole, so it still sounds formal and always suggests a crowd.
normalIntro.cn: furor 是英语原样借入的拉丁语名词，所以至今偏书面，且总暗示一群人。

normal.en: Furor and fury share the rage root, but furor names the crowd and fury names the temper.
normal.cn: furor 与 fury 同根，但 furor 指人群的怒气，fury 指个人的脾气。

normal.en: A furor is public: newspapers report it, and many people feel it at once.
normal.cn: furor 是公共的：报纸报道它，许多人同时感受到它。

normal.en: The phrase a furor over names the thing that set the crowd alight.
normal.cn: 短语 a furor over 后面接点燃人群的那件事。

normal.en: British English often writes furore, and the meaning does not change.
normal.cn: 英式英语常写作 furore，含义不变。

normal.en: A furor dies down, which is why the word suits scandals and short crazes.
normal.cn: furor 会平息，所以这个词适合丑闻与短暂的风潮。

abstract.en: Picture a crowded square where one shouted sentence turns every face red.
abstract.cn: 想象拥挤的广场上，一句喊出的话让每张脸都涨红。

abstract.en: Picture a new dance that sweeps a whole school in a single week.
abstract.cn: 想象一支新舞在一周之内席卷整所学校。

abstract.en: Picture one man running through empty streets at night, shouting at the moon.
abstract.cn: 想象一个男人在夜里跑过空街，对着月亮大喊。

examples.en: The minister resigned after a furor over his private emails.
examples.cn: 在一场因其私人邮件而起的哗然之后，这位部长辞职了。

examples.en: Her remarks provoked a furor in the press.
examples.cn: 她的言论在新闻界激起一片哗然。

examples.en: The play caused a furore when it first opened in London.
examples.cn: 这部戏在伦敦首演时引起轰动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「火炉」——furor 读起来像火炉，人群的怒气像炉火一样烧起来；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 furere（发狂）→ furor（狂乱、暴怒）→ 英语直接借入 furor；意大利语 furore 又带来英式拼写，核心义「众人共燃的狂怒」。

sensesIntro.en: Furor begins as rage shared by a whole public, widens into any hot craze, narrows back to the frenzy of one person, and ends in the old poetic sense of inspired madness.
sensesIntro.cn: furor 从整个公众共享的狂怒开始，扩展为任何热烈的风潮，再收窄到一个人的狂乱，最后落在古老的「诗兴迷狂」义上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one spark setting a whole crowd alight.
core.cn: 核心意象：一点火星点燃整片人群。

branches.en: Anger shared by the public is the leading sense.
branches.cn: 公众共享的愤怒是首要义项。

branches.en: The same heat turned toward a fashion gives the craze sense.
branches.cn: 同一份热度转向时尚，就有了风潮义项。

branches.en: The Latin madness narrows to the frenzy of one person.
branches.cn: 拉丁语中的「疯狂」收窄为一个人的狂乱。

branches.en: Inspired madness is the classical sense kept by poets.
branches.cn: 灵感式的迷狂是诗人保留的古典义项。

branches.en: A craze and a frenzy are both heat that has escaped control.
branches.cn: 风潮与狂乱都是失控的热度。

intro.en: Furor is built on the Latin rage root fur- plus the noun suffix -or, and the family spreads through fury, furious, and furore.
intro.cn: furor 由拉丁词根 fur-（狂怒）加名词后缀 -or 构成，词族延伸到 fury、furious 与 furore。

latinIntro.en: Latin furere means to rave, and furor is the noun of that state; furia and furiosus belong to the same family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 furere 意为「发狂」，furor 是表示这种状态的名词；furia 与 furiosus 同属这个词族。

items.example: The root fur- carries the heat of rage.
items.exampleCN: 词根 fur- 带着怒气的热度。

items.example: Furere is the verb behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: furere 是这个名字背后的动词。

items.example: Latin furor was borrowed whole into English.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 furor 被英语整体借入。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -or turns a verb of feeling into a noun of state.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -or 把表示感觉的动词变成状态名词。

items.example: Italian furore supplied the British spelling.
items.exampleCN: 意大利语 furore 提供了英式拼写。

items.example: Fury names the anger of one person.
items.exampleCN: fury 指一个人的狂怒。

items.example: Furious describes the angry person.
items.exampleCN: furious 描述发怒的人。

items.example: The suffix -ous forms furiosus and then furious.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ous 构成 furiosus，再变成 furious。

items.example: The prefix in- plus the rage root gives infuriate.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 加狂怒词根构成 infuriate。

definition_zh: 狂怒；暴怒；猛烈；激烈；复仇女神
definition_en: violent, uncontrolled anger, or the great force of a storm or struggle
core_image: 胸口烧起的火，眼睛都红了
scene: 母亲听说孩子被欺负，气得浑身发抖。Her voice shook with fury as she described the accident.
sceneCN: 这里 fury 是「狂怒」（第 1 个义项：难以控制的极度愤怒）；句意：她描述那场事故时，声音因狂怒而发抖。

pos.zh: 名词：狂怒；暴怒；猛烈；激烈；复仇女神

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀 -ious 构成，义为「狂怒的；猛烈的」
由形容词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「狂怒地；猛烈地」
由前缀 in- 加同源词根构成，义为「使大怒；激怒」

senses.title: Violent anger
senses.definition: a feeling of very strong anger that is hard to control
senses.definitionCN: 难以控制的极强烈愤怒
senses.example: She slammed the door in fury.
senses.exampleCN: 她怒气冲冲地摔上门。
senses.why: Latin furia names raging madness, so the noun begins with anger at fever heat rather than ordinary annoyance.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 furia 指狂乱的暴怒，所以这个名词从一开始就是高烧般的怒气，而不是普通的不快。

senses.title: A fit of anger
senses.definition: a short period of violent anger, especially one shown in action
senses.definitionCN: 一段短暂的暴怒，尤指表现在行动上的
senses.example: He flew into a fury and overturned the table.
senses.exampleCN: 他勃然大怒，掀翻了桌子。
senses.why: The word can name the whole episode, not only the feeling, so a fury is something a person enters and then leaves.
senses.whyCN: 这个词能指整段发作，而不只是感觉，所以 a fury 是人进入又离开的一段状态。

senses.title: Violent force of nature
senses.definition: the great force of a storm, wind, or sea
senses.definitionCN: 风暴、风或海面的巨大力量
senses.example: The fury of the hurricane flattened the harbour.
senses.exampleCN: 飓风的狂暴把港口夷为平地。
senses.why: The oldest picture of rage is a storm, and English lets weather borrow the word when its force looks like anger.
senses.whyCN: 怒气最古老的画面是风暴，当自然力看起来像发怒时，英语就让天气借用这个词。

senses.title: Extreme intensity
senses.definition: extreme force or intensity in a fight, attack, or activity
senses.definitionCN: 战斗、攻击或活动中极端的力度与强度
senses.example: The debate was fought with all the fury of a war.
senses.exampleCN: 那场辩论打得像战争一样激烈。
senses.why: When people fight, the heat of anger becomes the heat of the struggle, so fury can describe the intensity itself.
senses.whyCN: 人相争时，怒气的热度变成争斗的热度，所以 fury 也能描述强度本身。

senses.title: An avenging goddess
senses.definition: one of the goddesses of Greek and Roman myth who punished wrongdoing
senses.definitionCN: 希腊罗马神话中惩罚恶行的女神之一
senses.example: Orestes was pursued by the Furies.
senses.exampleCN: 俄瑞斯忒斯被复仇女神追逼。
senses.why: The Latin plural furiae named the goddesses of rage, and English keeps the capital letter for that mythic sense.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语复数 furiae 就是这些暴怒女神的名称，英语用大写保留这层神话义。

intro.en: Fury comes from Latin furia, raging madness, from furere, to rave; the same noun also named the avenging goddesses.
intro.cn: fury 来自拉丁语 furia（狂乱），源于 furere（发狂）；同一个名词也用来称呼复仇女神。

items.en: Furere means to rave and to lose control of the mind.
items.cn: furere 意为发狂、失去理智。

items.en: Furia means raging madness, and its plural furiae names the goddesses of rage.
items.cn: furia 意为狂乱的暴怒，复数 furiae 指暴怒女神。

items.en: Old French furie carries the word into French.
items.cn: 古法语 furie 把这个词带入法语。

items.en: Middle English fury keeps both the anger and the mythic goddesses.
items.cn: 中古英语 fury 同时保留怒气与神话女神的含义。

items.en: Modern English extends fury to storms and to any extreme intensity.
items.cn: 现代英语把 fury 扩展到风暴以及任何极端的强度。

note.en: Fury is the noun of rage, with furious and furiously as its own family and rage, wrath, and anger as its nearest neighbours.
note.cn: fury 是表示狂怒的名词，自己的词族有 furious 与 furiously，最近的邻居是 rage、wrath 与 anger。

entries.definition: extremely angry
in a violently angry way
angry public excitement
very strong anger that is hard to control
entries.definitionCN: 盛怒；暴怒（与 fury 最接近）

entries.definition: great angry indignation, often literary
entries.definitionCN: 愤怒；震怒（书面语，多指要惩罚的怒）

entries.definition: the general feeling of being displeased
entries.definitionCN: 生气；愤怒（最普通的说法）

normalIntro.en: Fury is the noun of the Latin rage root fur-, and furious, furiously, and furor all grow from it.
normalIntro.cn: fury 是拉丁词根 fur-（狂怒）的名词形式，furious、furiously 与 furor 都由它生长出来。

normal.en: Fury is the noun and furious is the adjective, so the pair describes the same heat.
normal.cn: fury 是名词，furious 是形容词，两者描述同一份热度。

normal.en: In a fury names the state a person is in, not just the feeling.
normal.cn: in a fury 指一个人所处的状态，而不只是感觉。

normal.en: The Furies take a capital letter because they are goddesses in myth.
normal.cn: the Furies 要大写，因为它们是神话里的女神。

normal.en: The fury of the storm moves the word from people to weather.
normal.cn: the fury of the storm 把这个词从人移到天气。

normal.en: Sound and fury is a famous phrase for noise that means nothing.
normal.cn: sound and fury 是名句，指毫无意义的喧闹。

abstract.en: Picture steam lifting a pot lid and rattling it hard.
abstract.cn: 想象蒸汽把锅盖顶起来，撞得直响。

abstract.en: Picture a fist hitting a wall and leaving a mark.
abstract.cn: 想象一拳打在墙上，留下痕迹。

abstract.en: Picture waves smashing a wooden pier until the planks break.
abstract.cn: 想象海浪猛撞木栈桥，直到木板断裂。

examples.en: He turned on his heel and walked out in a fury.
examples.cn: 他转身就走，怒气冲冲地离开了。

examples.en: The fury of the wind kept the boats in harbour.
examples.cn: 狂风的猛烈让船只都留在港内。

examples.en: Her eyes burned with fury when she heard the lie.
examples.cn: 听到那句谎话时，她的眼中燃着怒火。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「火里」——人像在火里，怒不可遏；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 furere（发狂）→ furia（狂乱；复数 furiae 亦指复仇女神）→ 古法语 furie → 中古英语 fury，核心义「烧到失控的怒气」。

sensesIntro.en: Fury starts as uncontrolled anger in one person, becomes a whole fit of rage, passes to the violent force of weather, then to any extreme intensity, and finally to the goddesses who embodied it.
sensesIntro.cn: fury 从一个人难以控制的愤怒开始，变成一整段暴怒发作，再转到天气的猛烈力量，然后泛指任何极端的强度，最后落到体现这种怒气的女神。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fire burning in the chest until the eyes turn red.
core.cn: 核心意象：胸中烧着一团火，直到眼睛发红。

branches.en: Uncontrolled anger is the core sense.
branches.cn: 难以控制的愤怒是核心义项。

branches.en: A fit is anger with a beginning and an end.
branches.cn: 暴怒发作是有着开头与结尾的怒气。

branches.en: Weather borrows the word when its force looks like rage.
branches.cn: 当自然力看起来像发怒时，天气就借用了这个词。

branches.en: Intensity in a struggle is anger turned into effort.
branches.cn: 争斗中的强度是怒气转化成的力量。

branches.en: A storm and a fierce debate share one scale of force.
branches.cn: 风暴与激烈的辩论共享同一把力量的标尺。

intro.en: Fury is the Latin noun of the rage root fur-, and the family runs through furia, furious, furiously, furor, and infuriate.
intro.cn: fury 是拉丁词根 fur-（狂怒）的名词形式，词族贯穿 furia、furious、furiously、furor 与 infuriate。

latinIntro.en: Latin furere means to rave, furia means raging madness, and the plural furiae names the goddesses of vengeance.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 furere 意为「发狂」，furia 意为「狂乱」，复数 furiae 指复仇女神。

items.exampleCN: 词根 fur- 带着怒气的热度。

items.example: Furere supplies the verb behind fury.
items.exampleCN: furere 提供 fury 背后的动词。

items.example: Furia is the direct source of fury.
items.exampleCN: furia 是 fury 的直接来源。

items.example: Furiae gives English the Furies.
items.exampleCN: furiae 给英语带来 the Furies 一词。

items.example: Furious is the adjective of fury.
items.exampleCN: furious 是 fury 的形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ious builds furious from the rage root.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ious 从狂怒词根构成 furious。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms furiously.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成 furiously。

items.example: Furor points the same rage at a crowd.
items.exampleCN: furor 把同样的怒气指向人群。

items.example: The prefix in- plus the rage root gives infuriate.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 加狂怒词根构成 infuriate。

definition_zh: 保险丝；导火索；熔接；融合；熔断
definition_en: a safety device that melts to break an electrical circuit, or to melt and join things into one whole
core_image: 两根金属丝在高温里熔成一根，细丝先烧断
scene: 台灯突然灭了，父亲打开插座旁的盒子，换上一根细丝。He replaced the blown fuse and the lamp came back on.
sceneCN: 这里 fuse 是「保险丝」（第 1 个义项：电路里的熔断保护元件）；句意：他换掉烧断的保险丝，灯又亮了。

pos.zh: 名词：保险丝；导火索；引信
动词：熔接；熔合；融合；（电路）熔断

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「熔合；融合；核聚变」
由本词加形容词后缀 -ible 构成，义为「可熔的；易熔的」
由前缀 de-（去除）加本词构成，义为「拆除引信；缓和局面」
由本词加表示施动者的后缀 -er 构成，义为「熔合装置；定影组件」

senses.title: Electrical safety device
senses.definition: a thin wire or small device that melts and breaks a circuit when the current is too strong
senses.definitionCN: 电流过强时会熔化并切断电路的细导线或小器件
senses.example: A fuse protects the wiring from overheating.
senses.exampleCN: 保险丝保护线路免于过热。
senses.why: The name came from the igniter cord, and the electrical part works the same way: a thin wire takes the heat and melts so the rest survives.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字来自点火用的引线，电路元件的工作方式也一样：细导线承受热量而熔断，其余部分得以保全。

senses.title: Igniter for an explosive
senses.definition: a cord or device that carries fire to an explosive charge
senses.definitionCN: 把火引到炸药装药处的导火线或装置
senses.example: The miner lit the fuse and ran for cover.
senses.exampleCN: 矿工点燃导火索，跑去找掩护。
senses.why: The oldest English fuse was a tube or cord of powder that carried flame, and the word still names that slow burning path.
senses.whyCN: 英语里最早的 fuse 是装火药、传递火焰的管子或绳索，这个词至今仍指那条缓慢燃烧的路径。

senses.title: To melt and join
senses.definition: to join pieces of metal or plastic by heating them until they melt together
senses.definitionCN: 把金属或塑料加热到熔化，使碎片接成一体
senses.example: Workers fused the pipes with a torch.
senses.exampleCN: 工人用喷灯把管子熔接起来。
senses.why: The Latin source means to pour and to melt, so the verb returns to the oldest action: heat two edges until they become one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语源头意为「倾倒、熔化」，动词因此回到最古老的动作：把两个边加热到合为一体。

senses.title: To combine into one whole
senses.definition: to unite separate things, ideas, or groups into a single whole
senses.definitionCN: 把分开的事物、想法或群体联合成一个整体
senses.example: The band fuses jazz and traditional drums.
senses.exampleCN: 这支乐队把爵士乐与传统鼓乐融合在一起。
senses.why: Melting two metals gives one new metal, and that picture transfers easily to styles, ideas, and groups that lose their separate edges.
senses.whyCN: 熔合两种金属会得到一种新金属，这幅画面很容易转到风格、想法与群体上，让它们失去各自的分界。

senses.title: To stop working when a fuse blows
senses.definition: of an electrical device: to stop working because a fuse has melted
senses.definitionCN: 指电器因保险丝熔化而停止工作
senses.example: The lights fused when the heater was switched on.
senses.exampleCN: 取暖器一开，灯就因保险丝熔断而灭了。
senses.why: This sense turns the noun into an event: the fuse does its job, the circuit dies, and the whole device is said to fuse.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项把名词变成事件：保险丝完成使命，电路断开，整个电器就被说成 fuse。

intro.en: Fuse joins two Latin strands: fusus, the past participle of fundere, to pour or melt, and fusus, a spindle, which gave the name of the igniter cord.
intro.cn: fuse 汇合了两条拉丁语线索：fundere（倾倒、熔化）的过去分词 fusus，以及意为「纺锤」的 fusus，后者带来了引火线的名称。

items.en: Fundere means to pour out or to melt metal.
items.cn: fundere 意为倒出或熔化金属。

items.en: Fusus, the past participle, means poured or melted; as a noun it also means a spindle.
items.cn: 过去分词 fusus 意为「倒出的、熔化的」；作名词时还指纺锤。

items.en: Italian fuso, a spindle, names the spindle-shaped cord that carried fire.
items.cn: 意大利语 fuso（纺锤）用来称呼纺锤形的引火绳。

items.en: English fuse first names the cord that fires a charge.
items.cn: 英语 fuse 最早指导火索。

items.en: The electrical fuse takes its name from the same melting wire.
items.cn: 电路保险丝因同样会熔化的导线而得名。

items.en: The verb revives the Latin sense and means to melt together, literally or figuratively.
items.cn: 动词恢复了拉丁语含义，表示字面或比喻意义上的熔合。

note.en: Fuse is a melting word, so the look-alike group holds fusion and fusible, while the near meaning group holds weld, merge, and melt.
note.cn: fuse 是一个「熔化」词，形近组收 fusion 与 fusible，近义组收 weld、merge 与 melt。

entries.definition: the act of melting or blending into one
entries.definitionCN: 熔合；融合（由 fuse 加名词后缀构成）

entries.definition: able to be melted
to remove the fuse from a bomb, or to calm a dangerous situation
entries.definitionCN: 拆除引信；缓和紧张局面（与 fuse 只差前缀）

entries.definition: to join metal by heat and pressure
to combine two things into one
entries.definitionCN: 合并；融合（多用于组织与概念）

entries.definition: to turn from solid to liquid under heat
entries.definitionCN: 熔化（只强调变化，不强调接合）

normalIntro.en: Every sense of fuse comes from one Latin idea, to melt, and the melting wire links the circuit part, the igniter, and the verb.
normalIntro.cn: fuse 的每个义项都来自同一个拉丁语概念「熔化」，熔化着的导线把电路元件、引火线与动词串在一起。

normal.en: Blow a fuse literally means the wire melts, and figuratively means a sudden rage.
normal.cn: blow a fuse 字面是导线熔化，比喻义是突然暴怒。

normal.en: A short fuse is a quick temper, borrowed from a fuse that burns fast.
normal.cn: a short fuse 指急躁的脾气，借自烧得快的导火索。

normal.en: Fusion is the noun and fusible means able to be melted, so the family stays on the same heat.
normal.cn: fusion 是名词，fusible 意为可熔的，整个词族都停在同一份热度上。

normal.en: Defuse keeps the fuse inside the word: de- means taking it away.
normal.cn: defuse 把 fuse 留在词里：前缀 de- 表示拿走。

normal.en: When styles fuse, the word borrows the metal image and drops the literal heat.
normal.cn: 风格 fuse 时，这个词借用了金属的意象，去掉了字面上的高温。

abstract.en: Picture a thin wire glowing red and snapping in two.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细导线烧红，然后断成两截。

abstract.en: Picture a spark running along a cord and reaching a box of powder.
abstract.cn: 想象一点火星沿绳子爬行，抵达火药箱。

abstract.en: Picture two metal rods melting at the tips and becoming one rod.

examples.en: Check the fuse before you blame the lamp.
examples.cn: 先检查保险丝，再怪台灯。

examples.en: The sculptor fused scrap metal into a tall figure.
examples.cn: 雕塑家把废金属熔成一座高大人像。

examples.en: Her two languages fuse into a single playful style.
examples.cn: 她的两种语言融合成一种俏皮的风格。

root: 拉丁语 fundere（倾倒、熔化）→ 过去分词 fusus（熔化的；纺锤）→ 意大利语 fuso 与法语 fusee → 英语 fuse；名词先指导火索与保险丝，动词再回到「熔合」的源头义。

sensesIntro.en: Fuse starts with the two melting objects of daily life, the circuit wire and the igniter cord, then releases the old Latin verb: melt and join metal, blend ideas, and finally describe a device dying when its wire melts.
sensesIntro.cn: fuse 从日常生活里两个会熔化的物件讲起——电路保险丝与导火索，然后放出古老的拉丁动词：熔化并接合金属、融合想法，最后描述电器因导线熔化而停摆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: heat turning two edges into one, or a thin wire melting apart.
core.cn: 核心意象：高温把两个边熔成一体，或一根细丝熔化断开。

branches.en: The circuit wire that melts on purpose is the first sense.
branches.cn: 故意熔断的电路导线是第一个义项。

branches.en: The cord that carries fire is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 传递火焰的引线是最古老的义项。

branches.en: Melting two edges into one is the literal verb.
branches.cn: 把两个边熔成一体是动词的字面义。

branches.en: Styles and ideas borrow the same melting picture.
branches.cn: 风格与想法借用了同一幅熔化的画面。

branches.en: A fuse that blows makes the whole device stop.
branches.cn: 保险丝熔断会让整个电器停摆。

intro.en: Fuse rests on the Latin melting root fus-, and the family spreads through fusion, fusible, defuse, and fuser.
intro.cn: fuse 立于拉丁语「熔化」词根 fus- 之上，词族延伸到 fusion、fusible、defuse 与 fuser。

latinIntro.en: Latin fundere means to pour or melt, its past participle fusus means poured or melted, and fusio means a pouring.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 fundere 意为倾倒或熔化，过去分词 fusus 意为「倒出的、熔化的」，fusio 意为「倾倒」。

items.example: The root fus- holds the heat of melting.
items.exampleCN: 词根 fus- 含有熔化的热度。

items.example: Fundere is the verb behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: fundere 是整个词族背后的动词。

items.example: Fusus supplies the shape of the English word.
items.exampleCN: fusus 提供英语词形的来源。

items.example: Fusio is the source of fusion.
items.exampleCN: fusio 是 fusion 的来源。

items.meaning: a melting safety wire or igniter
items.example: Fuse names the object that melts.
items.exampleCN: fuse 指会熔化的物件。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ion forms fusion.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ion 构成 fusion。

items.example: Fusion keeps the noun of the melting action.
items.exampleCN: fusion 保留熔化动作的名词形式。

items.example: The suffix -ible forms fusible.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ible 构成 fusible。

items.example: The prefix de- means away, so defuse means take the fuse away.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 de- 表示离开，所以 defuse 意为把引信拿走。

definition_zh: 融合；熔合；核聚变；混合产物；（政党的）联合
definition_en: the process of joining two or more things into one, especially by melting or blending
core_image: 两股金属熔液汇成一条，边界消失
scene: 厨房里，亚洲香料与法国酱汁被倒进同一口锅。The restaurant is known for its fusion of Thai spices and French sauces.
sceneCN: 这里 fusion 是「（风格的）融合」（第 3 个义项：把不同来源的风格混成一体）；句意：这家餐厅以泰式香料与法式酱汁的融合著称。

pos.zh: 名词：融合；熔合；核聚变；混合产物；联合

senses.title: Nuclear fusion
senses.definition: the process in which light atomic nuclei join to form a heavier nucleus and release energy
senses.definitionCN: 轻原子核结合成较重原子核并释放能量的过程
senses.example: The sun is powered by nuclear fusion.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳的能量来自核聚变。
senses.why: Two nuclei melt into one and release the heat that held them apart, so physics uses the oldest melting image for its most powerful joining.
senses.whyCN: 两个原子核熔成一个，并释放出原本把它们分开的能量，所以物理学用最古老的熔化意象来命名最强的结合。

senses.title: Melting together
senses.definition: the act of melting two materials so that they become a single mass
senses.definitionCN: 把两种材料熔化、使它们成为一体的动作
senses.example: Fusion of the two metals produced a strong alloy.
senses.exampleCN: 两种金属熔合后产生了一种坚固的合金。
senses.why: The Latin noun means a pouring, and metal that is poured together can no longer be separated; this is the literal centre of the word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语名词意为「倾倒」，倒在一起的金属再也分不开；这是这个词最字面的核心。

senses.title: Blending of styles
senses.definition: the combining of different styles, traditions, or types into one work or practice
senses.definitionCN: 把不同风格、传统或类型合成一件作品或一种做法
senses.example: Her music is a fusion of folk song and electronica.
senses.exampleCN: 她的音乐是民歌与电子乐的融合。
senses.why: When two traditions meet, neither survives unchanged, and the result looks like an alloy: a fusion of sounds, dishes, or designs.
senses.whyCN: 两种传统相遇时，谁都不会原样留存，结果就像合金：声音、菜肴或设计的融合。

senses.title: Union of groups or parties
senses.definition: the joining of separate organizations or groups into a single body
senses.definitionCN: 把分开的组织或团体合成一个机构
senses.example: The fusion of the two parties changed the parliament.
senses.exampleCN: 两党的联合改变了议会格局。
senses.why: Political fusion borrows the metal image for groups that give up separate names and act as one body.
senses.whyCN: 政治上的 fusion 借用金属意象，指放弃各自名称、作为一个机构行动的团体。

senses.title: Something produced by blending
senses.definition: a thing or work made by blending different elements
senses.definitionCN: 由不同元素混合而成的事物或作品
senses.example: The dish is a fusion of Italian and Japanese cooking.
senses.exampleCN: 这道菜是意大利烹饪与日本烹饪的融合体。
senses.why: Once the act is named, the result takes the same name, so a fusion can be the thing on the plate rather than the process.
senses.whyCN: 动作有了名称之后，结果也用同一个名称，所以 fusion 可以指盘中的成品，而不只是过程。

intro.en: Fusion comes from Latin fusio, a pouring or melting, from fundere, to pour; French passed the noun to English.
intro.cn: fusion 来自拉丁语 fusio（倾倒、熔化），源于 fundere（倾倒）；法语把这个名词传给英语。

items.en: Fundere means to pour out or to melt metal.
items.cn: fundere 意为倒出或熔化金属。

items.en: Fusio names the act of pouring or melting.
items.cn: fusio 指倾倒或熔化的动作。

items.en: French fusion carries the noun into technical and general use.
items.cn: 法语 fusion 把这个名词带入技术语与一般用语。

items.en: English borrows fusion for the melting of metals.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入 fusion，指金属的熔合。

items.en: Physics gives fusion the nuclear sense, joining light nuclei.
items.cn: 物理学赋予 fusion 核聚变含义，指轻核结合。

items.en: Modern English extends fusion to cuisines, music, and party politics.
items.cn: 现代英语把 fusion 扩展到菜系、音乐与政党政治。

note.en: Fusion is the noun of melting together, so the look-alike group holds fuse and fusible, while the near meaning group holds blend, merger, and alloy.
note.cn: fusion 是「熔合成一体」的名词，形近组收 fuse 与 fusible，近义组收 blend、merger 与 alloy。

normalIntro.en: Fusion is fuse plus the noun suffix -ion, so the word literally names the act of melting together.
normalIntro.cn: fusion 就是 fuse 加名词后缀 -ion，所以这个词字面上就是「熔合」这一动作的名称。

normal.en: Fusion is the noun and fuse is the verb, so one names the act and the other performs it.
normal.cn: fusion 是名词，fuse 是动词，一个命名动作，一个执行动作。

normal.en: Nuclear fusion joins light nuclei, borrowing the same picture of two things becoming one.
normal.cn: 核聚变结合轻原子核，借用的仍是「两物成一」的画面。

normal.en: Fusion cuisine puts two cooking traditions on a single plate.
normal.cn: fusion cuisine 把两种烹饪传统放进同一只盘子。

normal.en: A political fusion is a merger of parties, with no kitchen involved.
normal.cn: 政治上的 fusion 是政党的合并，与厨房无关。

normal.en: Fusible means able to melt, so the whole family stays on the same heat.
normal.cn: fusible 意为可熔的，整个词族都停在同一份热度上。

abstract.en: Picture two light nuclei colliding and flashing into a heavier one.
abstract.cn: 想象两个轻核相撞，闪一下合成较重的核。

abstract.en: Picture two streams of molten metal pouring into a single mould.
abstract.cn: 想象两股金属熔液倒进同一个模子。

abstract.en: Picture one plate holding both a hot curry and a cool cream sauce.
abstract.cn: 想象一只盘子里同时盛着辛辣咖喱与清凉奶油酱。

examples.en: The reactor aims to reproduce fusion on earth.
examples.cn: 这座反应堆的目标是在地球上重现聚变。

examples.en: The band is famous for a fusion of rock and Indian classical music.
examples.cn: 这支乐队以摇滚与印度古典音乐的融合闻名。

examples.en: Their fusion of old and new design won the prize.
examples.cn: 他们把新旧设计融合在一起，赢得了奖项。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费优神」——费力把两样东西融成一体的巧手，像有神助；这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 fundere（倾倒、熔化）→ fusio（倾倒、熔合）→ 法语 fusion → 英语 fusion，核心义「把分开的东西熔成一体」。

sensesIntro.en: Fusion begins with the grandest joining, nuclear fusion, returns to the literal melting of metals, widens to blended styles and merged parties, and ends with the blended thing itself.
sensesIntro.cn: fusion 从最宏大的结合「核聚变」开始，回到字面上的金属熔合，再扩展到混合的风格与合并的政党，最后落在混成之物本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two streams of molten metal meeting and losing their edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：两股金属熔液相遇，边界随之消失。

branches.en: Nuclear fusion is the joining of nuclei.
branches.cn: 核聚变是原子核的结合。

branches.en: Melting metal together is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 把金属熔在一起是字面义项。

branches.en: Styles blend the way metals do.
branches.cn: 风格的混合就像金属熔合。

branches.en: Parties merge into one body.
branches.cn: 政党合并成一个机构。

branches.en: The blend is both the act and the thing produced.
branches.cn: 融合既是动作，也是产出的成品。
